Picks and Parlays NFL handicapper Steve Seagrave breaks down his top NFL player prop picks for Week 4 across several of the biggest games on the schedule. This week’s NFL prop bets feature quarterback, running back, wide receiver and anytime touchdown props , including passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards and touchdown scorer markets. Whether you’re searching for NFL Week 4 player props, NFL prop predictions, NFL betting picks or the best NFL props today , this guide features six player prop bets involving Jordan Love, Jonathan Taylor, Chuba Hubbard, Jake Ferguson and more ! NFL Week 4 Quarterback Props NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #1 Jameis Winston New York Giants OVER 208.5 Passing Yards (-114) The New York Giants have been very conservative with Jameis Winston, and he’s finished with 118 and 111 passing yards, but we have to keep in mind that he didn’t start in Monday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams. Now Winston gets an opportunity against an Arizona Cardinals defense that ranks below average against the pass while allowing 247 yards per game and their two starting cornerbacks have an average PFF grade of 52.1. Jacoby Brissett and the Cardinals have been airing it out as they rank top 10 in pass frequency. We have seen all three opposing quarterbacks eclipse this number against Arizona including Brock Purdy (297), Drew Lock (235) and Justin Herbert (209). It’s time for Winston to go back to his roots as a gunslinger in what sets up as a low scoring game with a solid total of 44.5. NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #2 Jordan Love Green Bay Packers OVER 1.5 Touchdown Passes (+110) Jordan Love has thrown exactly two touchdown passes in each of his first two games of the season while averaging 281.3 passing yards per game. Without Josh Jacobs, the Green Bay Packers rushing attack has been non-existent as they rank DEAD LAST in rushing yards per attempt with only 3 yards per carry. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers run defense has been very stout as they rank 2nd with only 3.1 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay has only allowed four passing touchdowns through their first three games, but DeShaun Watson beat this line with two, and Kyler Murray and the Vikings led early on and kept things relatively conservative. Love and the Packers will find it easier to throw against a strong run defense and they have plenty of scoring options at their disposal. NFL Week 4 Running Back Props NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #1 Jonathan Taylor Indianapolis Colts OVER 90.5 Rushing Yards (-112) Jonathan Taylor has covered this line in 2 of his first 3 games of the season with 68, 92 and 98 yards for an average of 86 yards per game. The Indianapolis Colts have only handed the ball of on 44% of their offensive snaps, but Taylor has still seen amazing volume with 23, 24 and 19 rushing attempts. Indianapolis has an elite offensive line that currently ranks 6th in run blocking according to PFF. The Washington Commanders did a solid job keeping the lid on Seattle Seahawk and Dallas Cowboy running backs, but Saquon Barkley did run for 83 yards against them in Week 1. However, Washington’s linebacker core has been bit by the injury bug as Leo Chenal is out for the season (neck) and Frankie Luvu is dealing with a nagging groin injury. This game will be played overseas in London, and the Colts find themselves as -3.5-point favorites which should set Taylor up with a positive game script. NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #2 Chuba Hubbard Carolina Panthers OVER 18.5 Receiving Yards (-114) FD Chuba Hubbard has crushed this line in 2 of 3 games to open the 2026 NFL campaign with 28, 11 and 38 receiving yards (avg 25.7/game) despite only seeing 4, 2 and 3 targets. Those targets could increase in Week 4 as Xavier Legette is listed as doubtful and Jalen Coker is listed as questionable. The Detroit Lions rank 5th in blitz rate (42.6%) and Hubbard already thrived against a blitz happy Chicago Bears defense in a Week 1 (38 yards) game where his teammate Jonathan Brooks also logged a 48-yard reception in that contest. Brooks has already been ruled out for the remainder of the season and that leaves Hubbard as the Panthers only legitimate receiving threat out of the backfield. We have already seen two running backs beat this number as Breece Hall finished with 23 yards and Travis Etienne finished with 32 yards. NFL Week 4 Wide Receiver/Tight End Props NFL Week 4 TE Prop Prediction Jake Ferguson Dallas Cowboys OVER 23.5 Receiving Yards (-114) In the first three weeks of the season, Jake Ferguson has run 82 routes while playing 128 snaps and posting a 10.9% target share in the process. Those are solid numbers while competing with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and Ferguson’s numbers are on the rise during the past two weeks while catching 7/9 targets for 66 yards. Now Ferguson draws an elite matchup against a Houston Texans defense that has allowed the 5th most yards (71/game) and 9th most receptions (6/game) to opposing tight ends. The Texans linebacking core is thin and most of their top coverage guys are banged up or ruled out for Week 4. We have already watched two tight ends absolutely torch Houston including Tyler Warren (55) and Dalton Kincaid (130). NFL Week 4 WR Prop Prediction Malik Washington Miami Dolphins OVER 37.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Malik Washington currently leads the Miami Dolphins in receiving yards (152), receptions (12) and targets (23) through the first three games of the season. More importantly to this particular play, Washington has covered this line in all three of those games with 56, 53 and 43 receiving yards. Now Washington will face off against a Minnesota Vikings defense that has allowed the 10th most receiving yards to opposing wide receivers with an average of 174 yards per game. We have already seen six opposing wide receivers eclipse this number against Minnesota including Emeka Egbuka (62), Ted Hurst III (40), Kalif Raymond (43), Rome Odunze (40), Matthew Golden (95) and Christian Watson (147). De’Von Achane is on the shelf due to an injury so there will be extra touches on the table, and the game script is perfect as the Dolphins sit as -10.5-point underdogs. NFL Week 4 Touchdown Props NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #1 James Cook III Buffalo Bills (-111) James Cook has scored in each of his last two games despite Josh Allen receiving 55.6% of the Buffalo Bills carries inside the five-yard line. Cook is the only other Bills player who has recorded a carry inside the five-yard line and Allen took a shot to the knee in Week 3 so he may be less likely to risk running in Week 4. Cook has scored a touchdown in 3 of his last 4 head-to-head meetings with the New England Patriots (6 total), and they just allowed both Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez scored against them in a blowout loss in Jacksonville. Cook has posted a monster 22.6% explosive run rate, so he doesn’t necessarily need to rely on scoring from the red area. The Bills are -6.5-point home favorites in this contest and that sets Cook up with an ideal game script to find the end zone. NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #2 Brock Bowers Las Vegas Raiders (+185) Brock Bowers had an amazing first game his 2026 campaign where he caught 10 of 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints. In that game, Bowers saw three red area targets while posting a 39.4% target share. Now Bowers gets an opportunity to expose a Kansas City Chiefs defense that has already allowed touchdowns to tight ends Evan Engram and Tyler Warren to score in 2026. The last time Bowers faced Kansas City was back in 2024 and he caught 10 of 14 targets for 140 yards and a touchdown despite playing on the road. Now he’s at home in an indoor game as a -4.5-point underdog which sets up for a pass heavy game script. By Zachary Cohen - October 3, 2026 88790 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 4 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 4 NFL best bets and Week 4 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders – 9:30 am ET (London) The Colts might be down Alec Pierce, but I like the way this offense operates. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. Bet: Over 46.5 (-115) Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans – 1:00 pm ET We haven’t seen anything from Houston this season, but a bounce-back performance should be coming soon. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. That said, look for Houston to start playing some much better defense, and we could see it start with a decent showing against Dak Prescott and Co. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). The Cowboys made some moves to address their miserable defense from last season, but it doesn’t look like any of them have worked. So, this should be a pretty strong matchup for CJ Stroud. Of course, Stroud has issues as a passer, but he’s reliable when he has time to get his feet set. That’s a good thing as Stroud prepares to face a defense that is 31st in Pass Rush Win Rate (40%). He should have plenty of time. This is also a massive desperation spot for Houston. I can’t imagine Dallas is thrilled to be sitting at 1-2 right now, but Houston’s season might be over if the team drops this one to fall to 0-4. Bet: Texans ML (-136) Arizona Cardinals at New York Giants – 1:00 pm ET Jameis Winston has been pretty buttoned up since taking over for Jaxson Dart, but I imagine he’ll be slinging it around a bit here. This season, the Cardinals are allowing 247.0 passing yards per game, and their two starting corners have an average PFF grade of 52.1. New York has been conservative with Winston so far, opting to lean heavily into a ground-and-pound approach. However, the Giants need to play the matchup, and this is one that calls for some passing. Arizona is a top-10 team in pass frequency. So, if the Cardinals are letting Jacoby Brissett air it out, the Giants will have no choice but to let Winston do the same. I know Winston hasn’t yet thrown for a score, and he also hasn’t eclipsed 118 passing yards in a game. But we all know that Winston is a gunslinger, and you don’t have to go back too far to find a box score in which he threw for 366 yards and two touchdowns. That was November 23, 2025, when Winston got involved in a shootout with the Lions. Follow on X Multiple Authors Oct 2, 2026, 11:00 AM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: find betting value. Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. From spreads and moneylines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 4. Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Jump to: Bowen's Game of the Week | Solak's plays | Walder's props Bowen's Game of the Week New England Patriots at Buffalo Bills (-6.5, 48.5) 1 p.m. ET on CBS, Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park, New York Josh Allen and the Bills split their series with the Patriots last season. Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire The Buffalo Bills , the AFC favorite to reach the Super Bowl, will host last season's AFC Super Bowl representative, the New England Patriots , in a matchup of AFC East rivals Sunday. The Patriots will need game plan answers on both sides of the ball to counter the Bills' high-scoring offense, and they'll have to create a more defined passing game without A.J. Brown (ankle) on the field. I like the Bills to win and cover in this one, and in a divisional game with this level of coaching and familiarity, I'll take the under on the total. Let's check out both clubs, and I'll add some props at the end to play, too. NFL betting • Survivor pools: Calm after early storm? • Survivor strategy: Take Jags, Texans • Best bets for Thanksgiving Day games • Odds for Week 12 games | Early bets • Purdy jumps Allen, trails Burrow for MVP • Super Bowl odds: 49ers alone at the top • Betting home | Super Bowl on ESPN When the Bills have the ball: In their Week 3 win over the Chargers, the Bills failed to control offensive tempo, and they turned the ball over. It happens in this league. But don't let one game change the narrative on an explosive Bills offense leading the NFL in scoring (33.7 PPG) and producing top-10 numbers in both passing and rushing. Quarterback Josh Allen will see heavy single-high coverage from New England (both man and zone), which creates opportunities for the Bills to scheme for crossing concepts and big-play throws on deep over routes, and they can also attack the seams with tight end Dalton Kincaid . The man matchup to watch to here is DJ Moore against Christian Gonzalez (shoulder), if the Patriots corner is up for the game. Best versus best. And let's not forget the offensive balance the Bills have with running back James Cook III , who has produced back-to-back games with at least 135 yards rushing, against a New England defense allowing 4.8 YPC. The question I always have for teams versus Allen, given his dual-threat ability, is how much man coverage can you play? And what is your answer for Allen as a runner in the low red zone? Let's see how the Patriots counter, as Allen has rushed for two scores in all three games played this season. He's the league's ultimate difference-maker. When the Patriots have the ball: Quarterback Drake Maye has made some reckless decisions with the ball, throwing a league-high six interceptions and registering a 45.9 QBR (25th in the league). But I'm not going to put this all on Maye, as the Patriots' wide receiver group is lacking juice and matchup edges. With Brown on IR, who is the boundary X to win the one-on-ones? The tape shows us that the New England wideouts aren't creating separation at a high rate. The key here is for Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels to scheme more defined throws -- while having answers to pressure -- versus a Bills defense that has been more zone-heavy (65.9% of opponent dropbacks). Maye is going to see split-safety coverage. Lift the safeties here and create those middle-of-the-field voids for the quarterback to drive the ball. More importantly, the Patriots need to generate some run-game efficiency with Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson to get the Bills out of two-deep coverage. The Patriots are averaging 3.9 YPC (20th in the league) with an explosive run rate of 8.2% (25th). No question on the numbers here. They are down. Let's see how McDaniels game-plans for Jim Leonhard and the Bills' new defensive scheme to get his QB rolling again. And it wouldn't surprise me if the Patriots try to muddy this one up with a ball control/play-action script. Now, let's get to some prop bets ... James Cook III is coming off two straight big rushing performances and is averaging 6.0 YPC. AP Photo/Adrian Kraus James Cook III rushing yards OVER 88.5 (-111) As mentioned, Cook has rushed for 135-plus in two straight, and he's averaging 19.3 carries per game. Plus, Cook has 12 rushes of 10 or more yards this season. Take the steady volume and the explosive-play ability here. Hunter Henry receiving yards OVER 30.5 (-110) Henry has topped the 31-yard mark just once this season, and he was held to just one reception in the Week 3 loss to Jacksonville. However, I see the tight end as an answer to the two-high zone coverage of the Bills. Henry can be the outlet for Maye, while also pressing the seams. DJ Moore receptions OVER 3.5 (-133) The juice isn't friendly on this one, but that's a low reception total for Moore. In the two full games Moore has played (he left Week 2 early with an injury), he had at least five receptions in both. Look for the Bills to use motion to deploy Moore, getting him free access off the ball versus man coverage. Scott W. Grau/Icon Sportswire Detroit Lions -3.5 (-112) at Carolina Panthers It's important to watch the forecast for this game as we get closer to kickoff. There's a good chance of rain showers Sunday night, and we know that Jared Goff 's performance as a passer can be impacted more by bad weather, given his smaller hands. But I still feel comfortable taking this bet at this number because of the Panthers' injury issues. Both starting cornerbacks are expected to miss this game, which all but precludes Carolina from playing man coverage against Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams . If the Panthers take a zone-heavy approach, expect Jahmyr Gibbs to run wild -- heck, expect Gibbs to run wild anyway, as the Panthers are giving up more rushing yards per game to running backs than any other defense. Have I mentioned the Panthers' passing defense is also among the league worst against tight ends? The Lions have Carolina outgunned offensively, and I'm not sure Bryce Young can keep scoring pace. Receiver Jalen Coker (quad) is questionable, three starting offensive linemen ( Ikem Ekwonu , Damien Lewis and Taylor Moton ) are out, and a key backup ( Monroe Freeling ) is in concussion protocol. Detroit's defense is extremely gettable through the air, but the Lions have enough pass rush power to generate sacks and turnovers such that the Panthers can't keep this shootout within one score. Los Angeles Rams -3 (-115) at Philadelphia Eagles Editor's Picks Top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 4 Mike Clay NFL Week 4 betting: Odds, lines and totals for every game Early bets for Week 4: Four games to target right away ESPN 2 Related I would only take this line at -3 (up to -120) and not buy the hook, so move quickly here. DeVonta Smith missed practice Thursday with his hamstring injury, which officially moves him into the "seriously questionable" category as we approach Sunday. I already leaned to the Rams' side with a healthy Smith. If he can't go, the Eagles' receiver corps will feature Dontayvion Wicks , first-round rookie Makai Lemon and Hollywood Brown against the loaded Rams secondary. Remember, pass-catching tight end Dallas Goedert is also out with a knee injury. The Eagles' defense had a brutal night last Monday against the Chicago Bears ' passing attack, regularly suffering communication issues as the Bears sent receivers in motion. They get another motion-heavy passing attack in Sean McVay's Rams offense, which gets Puka Nacua back at a critical time -- at 1-2, the Rams need a road win to prevent the sirens from screaming in their Super Bowl-aspiring season. They also have a vengeance play here, as they gave up a big second-half lead to the Eagles last season ... then lost the game on a would-be game-winning field goal that was blocked by Jordan Davis . The Eagles simply have too many personnel deficiencies to ignore against a team as deep and talented as the Rams. Get this line before Smith news pushes it higher before kickoff. Miami Dolphins team total points UNDER 13.5 (-115) Minnesota Vikings DC Brian Flores is calling defense for the first time against his old team. He has downplayed the importance of facing Miami, but I'd imagine the leaders in the locker room know how big of a game this is for their top-flight coordinator. I also think this is about as big of a mismatch as we will see this season. The Dolphins are without running back De'Von Achane , who provided much-needed game-breaking ability from the running back spot. Without him, the Dolphins' best chance for chunk gains will come from the passing game, which is a scary proposition against Flores' blitz-heavy approach. Bobby Slowik, the new offensive coordinator in Miami, lost his job in Houston in large part due to predictable protection rules that were easily exploited by opposing defensive coordinators -- and no coach has been better attacking the Mike Shanahan system in pass protection than Flores. I'm tracking under 13.5 at -115 for a full unit and under 7.5 points at +285 for a half unit. A shutout at 13-1 would be fun, but that's too short of a price to take seriously. Omarion Hampton rushing yards UNDER 45.5 (-109) NFL Pick 'Em FREE to play. Create up to 10 entries and compete for 58 prizes worth $102K. Make Your Picks Hampton's share of carries took a hit last week, as he saw 57.7% of the designed rushes after holding 76.7% and 75.0% in the first two weeks of the season, respectively. The Los Angeles Chargers wanted to get Keaton Mitchell more involved as they looked for any sort of juice on offense, and it was a better day for the running game overall. I expect a time share moving forward. But it will be a tough test against the Seattle Seahawks , who boast the best run-defending line in football. There might be no greater mismatch in Week 4 than the Chargers' interior offensive line against defensive tackles Byron Murphy II and Leonard Williams . If the Chargers are to find any success on the ground, they'll need to get the ball to the boundary -- those are the Mitchell plays, not the Hampton plays. The Chargers were able to run the ball a lot more last week as they tripped into an early lead after the Bills' many turnovers, but it's more likely they get stuck in a trailing game script in this one. Hampton has big-play ability if he breaks into space, so taking the under on attempts might be a safer approach. I didn't want to pay the juice at under 13.5 attempts at -123 as of this posting, but if under 12.5 appears, I'll be interested in taking that. Kaleb Johnson rushing attempts OVER 8.5 (-115) The Green Bay Packers ' lack of a handoff game is harrowing. Through three games, the Packers have 146 total rushing yards from running backs -- eighth fewest for a team through three games over the past six seasons. The one-dimensionality on offense particularly haunted them against the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday night, but they've had a long week to explore offensive line reinforcements and recommit to the rushing attack. Green Bay has the fifth-highest pass rate over expectation per Next Gen Stats. Behind that offensive line? No shot. They need to find a rushing attack, and they know it. Critically, the Packers draw a rookie UDFA quarterback ( Jalon Daniels ) making his first career start for a bad Tampa Bay Buccaneers team. The potential to build an actual lead and salt it away should also increase the total handoffs in this game. The Packers clearly don't trust MarShawn Lloyd as a ball carrier, and Chris Brooks is the third-down back. If the running game plays a bigger role this week in a leading game script, Johnson is the most likely beneficiary. I prefer Johnson's attempts to his yardage totals, simply because the Packers' line is still a problem. But both are bettable as his role expands. Woody Marks rushing yards OVER 33.5 (-114) NFL Win Totals Predict OVER or UNDER for every team's win total. FREE to play. $5K in prizes! Make Your Picks Our Dan Graziano reported this week that his sense of the Houston Texans ' running game is that more work should go Marks' way . I'm inclined to agree. David Montgomery is a good stay-ahead-of-the-sticks rusher, but with Houston's offensive line issues, he has been unable to solve their short-yardage problems on his own. By getting the ball to Marks on the outside, the Texans can find bigger runs without worrying as much about their interior offensive line play. The Dallas Cowboys have given up 114.3 rushing yards per game to running backs through three weeks, fifth worst in the league. They have played three mobile QBs ( Jaxson Dart , Jayden Daniels , Lamar Jackson ) who make run defense more challenging, but the eye test confirms the liability of players like outside linebackers Rashan Gary and Donovan Ezeiruaku in setting a hard edge. With Nico Collins back in the starting lineup for Houston, the temptation is to think the Texans will become more pass-heavy -- but their offensive philosophy this season was always to give C.J. Stroud a better running game. I'd take Marks to 36.5 this week, and I'd look at some longest rush props as well. Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures . Zay Flowers receiving yards OVER 66.5 (-110) I had all sorts of Flowers overs to target against the Cowboys last week, but his hamstring injury limited him to just 15 routes. Of course, he still went over his yardage prop with 84 yards on only 15 routes. Flowers is a huge-play star-in-the-making in this Declan Doyle offense, and the books still haven't caught up. Flowers has now only played 1.5 games of football through three weeks, and four of those six quarters were with load management. Yet, he has 234 receiving yards and a whopping 9.36 yards per route run because of how easily the Baltimore Ravens are getting him open with motion, backfield alignment and play-action pass fakes. He's as central to this passing attack as Jaxon Smith-Njigba is to Seattle's, and as he strings together full healthy games, we'll never see a number in the 60s for him again. If you're worried about continued management on the hamstring injury, especially in a game the Ravens might dominate, consider taking Flowers' first-quarter receiving props (over 14.5 receiving yards is +100) to ensure the Ravens are still in their base offense. Michael Mayer receiving yards OVER 21.5 (-116) In Brock Bowers ' first game back healthy, Mayer's route share was totally unaffected. Mayer ran a route on 71% of the Las Vegas Raiders ' dropbacks in Week 1, 72% in Week 2, and 70% in Week 3. That's because the Raiders are using Bowers like a true wide receiver. They were in multiple-TE sets on over 80% of their total snaps, and with Bowers typically in slot or wide alignments, Mayer got the matchups against linebackers and safeties from his traditional inline alignments. Throw in the fact that the Raiders' traditional wide receivers are a thin group without much demand for targets, and I still think Mayer is the second target after Bowers. As opposing defenses spend more resources to take Bowers out of the game plan, it's Mayer who will benefit. The Raiders have a good shot of a trailing game script against the Kansas City Chiefs . The Chiefs' run-heavy approach shortens the clock and makes it a little tougher to take receptions, so I prefer receiving yards here. But if we get into a big score deficit in the second half, I'll look for a live receptions over on Mayer. Ben Solak 2026 best bets record Category Record Unit change Spread 5-9 -4.4 Total 1-2 -1.1 Passing props 8-5 +3.5 Receiving props 6-12 -6.6 Rushing props 8-2 +5.3 Rushing and receiving props 0-1 -1.0 Touchdown props 1-2 -1.1 Overall 29-33 -5.6 Walder's prop bets Note: More defensive props will be added as odds become available Defensive plays Miami Dolphins to record first sack of game (+170) On one hand, this is bold because the Dolphins have not sacked the quarterback this season. Not once. On the other hand, maybe it's not that bold, because the Minnesota Vikings have taken sacks at the second-highest rate in the NFL (10.2%). Granted, that was partially with Carson Wentz in the lineup, and now Minnesota has a more mobile Kyler Murray back. But still, my belief has always been that the quarterback and offense control sacks more than the defense. I spun up a new model for this category just this week, and it seems like it agrees, considering it has the Dolphins as a plus-money value. Arizona Cardinals to NOT give up a sack on their first drive (-411) NFL Playoff Predictor Predict the final standings in every division, then choose which teams will earn a wild-card berth! FREE to play. Make Your Picks One of the biggest disappointments of the season thus far has been a New York Giants pass rush that has managed a 1.0% sack rate, second worst among all teams. Their pass rush win rate tells a similar story; it ranks 25th best. Now, the Cardinals' pass protection has also not been good this year, ranking second worst in pass block win rate. Despite that, they have allowed sacks on just 4.1% of dropbacks, better than the league average of 6.0%. My model believes their chances of giving up a sack on their opening drive is quite a bit lower than these odds suggest. Greg Rousseau under 0.75 sacks (+147) Rousseau is having an unbelievable start to the season, with 6.0 sacks in three games. It's a huge jump in sack pace for him: he's never recorded more than 8.0 sacks in a season. While Rousseau probably has improved, the model is skeptical he's improved as much as these odds imply. A big reason why? His pass rush win rate still isn't that great. A year ago Rousseau was in the 16th percentile in the metric at edge. Now, he's the 30th percentile. Better, sure, but it still suggests he isn't winning on a down-to-down basis as much as top-flight pass rushers. And that reduces his sack forecast going forward. I would bet this down to even money. Jermaine Johnson II over 0.25 sacks (+275) I've been a long-time Johnson skeptic, but this line has pushed the hate so far that I'm on his side now. One factor is the quarterback he's facing: Lamar Jackson . The Ravens' quarterback has taken sacks at an average-ish 5.7% clip this year, but my model isn't ready to totally forget the massive 9.8% number he recorded a year ago. And even if you don't think Johnson is great -- and I don't -- he's still on the field on 66% of the Titans' pass rushes and 77% in clear passing situations. This line is too good to pass up. I would bet this down to +175. It's the first number that stands out, because it ranks in the 84th percentile among safeties. But here's the thing: the 49ers have been pass-heavy this season! They literally rank first in pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. And every time a Broncos opponent opts to pass instead of run, that cuts Jones' chances of recording a tackle roughly in half. That's one reason why my model likes Jones' under quite a bit. I would bet this down to -132. Roquan Smith over 7.5 tackles + assists (+102) This is a low tackle line for Smith to clear, considering he's gone over 7.5 in each of his three games this season and nine out of 15 last year. On one hand, we can understand why: the Ravens are huge favorites over the Titans, and so the game script expectation is that Tennessee will fall behind and be forced to pass. For a linebacker like Smith, that would be bad for his tackling numbers since he's much more likely to record one against the run. But working in our favor is that Tennessee has been extremely run heavy thus far, ranking 31st in pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats. My attempts model assumes that is going to come down, because leaning that heavily on the pass game is not what the Packers have done in the past under Matt LaFleur. Green Bay ranked 26th in the same category last season. But there's also this: The Packers' offensive line has struggled immensely. I can only imagine they would want to limit the number of times Love drops back on Sunday, especially against Tampa Bay Buccaneers coach Todd Bowles, who loves to blitz. Jaylen Wright receptions OVER 1.5 (+180) Wright and Ollie Gordon II will handle the backfield workload in the wake of De'Von Achane's season-ending ACL injury. Both have almost no experience catching the ball in the pros, but someone is going to have to catch passes out of the backfield -- and that's especially true this week. That's because the Miami Dolphins are playing the Minnesota Vikings, one of the most zone-heavy teams in the league (78% zone). Running backs catch passes against zone coverage almost twice as frequently compared to when they face man coverage, and in my back tests, betting the receptions over on running backs facing zone-heavy defenses has been profitable. Betting “against the spread” refers to the act of choosing the winning team based on a numeric handicap placed on the team that oddsmakers believe is superior, rather than picking the outright winner. For example, if the Rams face the Bengals, and oddsmakers set the spread at Rams -3.5, you would need Los Angeles to win by 4 or more points in order to cash your Rams bet. What is an Over/Under Bet? Over/Under is a wager based on how many points you think will be scored in a specific game. Oddsmakers set the total, and bettors decide whether the final score will be higher or lower than that number. If an Over/Under is set at 44.5 points and you bet Over, you will need the combined score of both teams to be 45 points or higher to win your bet. What is a Moneyline Bet? A moneyline bet involves choosing which team you believe will win a specific matchup. The moneyline favorite carries a minus designation, like -130. This means that you need to wager $130 to earn a $100 profit. Conversely, the underdog carries a plus designation, like +110. This means that you win $110 in profit on a $100 bet. articles.text: 2026 NFL Week 4 Picks: Best Bets For Every Game — Will's Wagers | FOX Sports my favs Access and manage your favorites here DISMISS Scores Watch Betting Stories Search Sign In Account SPORTS & TEAMS PLAYERS SHOWS PERSONALITIES TOPICS POPULAR SEARCHES - No Data Available - BROWSE BY SPORTS & TEAMS PLAYERS SHOWS PERSONALITIES TOPICS Built on National Football League National Football League Add FOX Sports on Google 2026 NFL Week 4 Picks: Best Bets For Every Game — Will's Wagers Published Oct. 1, 2026 1:55 p.m. ET share facebook x reddit link Will Hill FOX Sports Betting Analyst There are several barnburners on tap for NFL Week 4. Here's where I'm putting my money. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . Steelers @ Browns Pittsburgh coach Mike McCarthy said he wanted to push the ball down the field more this year than the team did last year with Aaron Rodgers, and he has been true to his word so far. Rodgers’ average depth of target has been over 10 yards in two of the three games so far, including in a 30-27 win last week. I’ll go over the 38.5, as the Steelers take on a Browns team with some interesting young weapons and an underrated offense. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 Colts @ Commanders Don’t forget to set your alarms for this one, as we get our first 9:30 am ET kickoff of the season in London come Sunday. Both teams started 0-2 before winning in Week 3. With the winner getting to .500, I’ll take the 3.5 with the Commanders in what should be a close game. Hill's Pick: Commanders +3.5 Patriots @ Bills It has not been pretty for the defending AFC champions, but it’s often a good idea to ignore the last thing you saw in the NFL to avoid overreacting. The Patriots will already be 3.5 games out of first place in the AFC East with a loss. They are desperate and getting 6.5 points. I’l bet on them to bounce back. Hill's Pick: Patriots +6.5 Titans @ Ravens If the Titans aren’t the worst team in the NFL, they’re pretty close to it. At 0-3, their offense has been anemic, and I don’t expect it to improve this week in Baltimore. Hill's Pick: Titans Under 15.5 Jaguars @ Bengals The quarterbacks for this game are familiar with each other. Trevor Lawrence and Joe Burrow were picked first overall, respectively, in back-to-back years (2020 and 2021), and also played against each other in the 2019 college football national title game. The Jaguars look like a contender and could easily be 3-0. In a toss-up game, I’ll take the points. Hill's Pick: Jaguars +2.5 Rams @ Eagles Panic time could officially hit the Rams if they lose again this week and fall to 1-3. The Eagles have had their number recently, winning all four meetings since the start of the 2023 season, and winning in Philadelphia isn’t easy, especially considering the onerous travel the Rams have endured already this season. Hill's Pick: Eagles +3 Cardinals @ Giants The Giants are 2-1, but their offense has looked suspect since quarterback Jaxson Dart went down with a season-ending knee injury. With the total set at 44.5, I think we get a 23-20 type of game. I will go Under here considering the Giants' lackluster offense. Hill's Pick: Under 44.5 Cowboys @ Texans The Cowboys’ defense was expected to be improved in 2026 after being dreadful in 2025, but we have yet to see that play out. The Cowboys' elite offense and shaky defense make them a good Over team until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 48.5 Jets @ Bears The Jets lost and failed to cover last week vs. the Lions, but were tied with just a few minutes to go. Quarterback Geno Smith has played very well for the Jets, and I think they will keep it close this week against the Bears. Hill's Pick: Jets +3.5 Packers @ Buccaneers Two desperate teams facing off here with each in dire need of a win. Undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels will make his first career start for the Buccaneers, and I expect points to be hard to come by. Hill's Pick: Under 38.5 Dolphins @ Vikings The Vikings look to improve to 4-0 and are heavy favorites to do so against the hapless Dolphins. While it’s been an impressive start for the Vikings, they have struggled mightily on offense, and aren’t well-equipped to exploit the Dolphins’ weak secondary. Star wide receiver Justin Jefferson might be sidelined for this one, and 10.5 points is a lot to lay for a struggling Vikings offense. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +10.5 Chiefs @ Raiders Raiders’ tight end Brock Bowers is one of the best, and perhaps, still one of the most underrated players in the league. Coming off of 13 targets, 10 catches and 116 yards in his season debut, expect another big game from Bowers. Hill's Pick: Brock Bowers Over 76.5 Receiving Yards Chargers @ Seahawks The Chargers look broken offensively and could not defeat the Bills last week despite their defense forcing five turnovers. I don’t look for them to do much offensively on the road, in a hostile environment against an angry Seahawks defense coming off an upset loss to the Commanders. Hill's Pick: Chargers Under 17.5 Broncos @ 49ers The 49ers are undefeated and have been ultra impressive so far, but as usual, the injuries are starting to pile up. In what should be a close game, I’ll take the Broncos to keep it close. Hill's Pick: Broncos +3 Lions @ Panthers The Lions have played three games and they’ve all gone Over. With an elite offense and very suspect defense, I like another Lions Over. Hill's Pick: Over 51.5 Falcons @ Saints The Saints gave up over 100 yards rushing last week and now face perhaps the most dynamic running back in the NFL. Look for Bijan Robinson to have another big game on the ground. That's where our Featured Pros come in. We asked a panel of sharp analysts to break down their favorite NFL Draft prop bets, highlighting where the value lies and which lines may be mispriced as draft buzz heats up. Whether you're targeting early-round chaos or late-round sleepers, these expert-backed picks can help you stay one step ahead on draft night. Please include the odds with your selection. Rueben Bain Jr. to be a Top 10 pick: Yes ( -162 ) “Miami Hurricanes EDGE Rueben Bain Jr. has 30.9-inch arms, which likely cause him to slide, but I don't think he can get past eight overall to the New Orleans Saints or nine overall to the Kansas City Chiefs. The 21-year-old finished fifth in the ACC with 7.5 sacks as a freshman, before regressing somewhat as a sophomore while battling injuries. Bain Jr. then returned to form this past year, setting career-highs in tackles (54), tackles for loss (15.5), and sacks (9.5), while leading the Hurricanes to a College Football Playoff (CFP) National Championship appearance. This earned him AP Consensus All-America and ACC Defensive Player of the Year honors, as well as the Ted Hendricks Award. Those accomplishments, a high character, and elite film should be enough to keep him inside the top 10 picks, making this arguably the best prop bet available.” – Seth Woolcock ( FantasyPros ) Jacob Rodriguez drafted inside the top-32 ( +500 ) “I’m a sucker for the “Will this player be drafted in Round 1″ betting market. Right now, my favorite approach is to select Texas Tech LB Jacob Rodriguez inside the top-32 at 5-1 odds. He’s been a buzzy late 1st-round pick across several sources (Tony Pauline) and has been tied to several teams between picks 15-32, such as Dallas, Houston, Miami, Buffalo, Pittsburgh, Tampa Bay, New England, and Chicago.” – Andrew Erickson ( FantasyPros ) Who will be the fourth overall pick? “Arvell Reese ( +650 at DraftKings ) or Sonny Styles ( +175 at BetMGM ) — The info/draft rumors I hear about change literally by the minute. By the time you read this, things might be drastically different, but here goes nothing. (FYI- at the time of this writing, it’s Wednesday night, 10:30 p.m.) Anyway, it sounds like Arizona’s owner, Michael Bidwell, might veto GM Monte Ossenfort’s wishes to trade out of the third pick. The rumor is that Ossenfort apparently either wants Edge David Bailey if he’s there or to trade it for more picks if the Jets select Bailey. However, Bidwell wants Jeremiyah Love because he would add some excitement to the Cardinals’ fan base and could help sell some tickets. So, if you think Arizona keeps the pick and selects Love, I think the best way to play that would be to bet the Titans to select Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles. I don’t think Titans’ head coach Robert Saleh (who is a former defensive coordinator) would take Love, Carnell Tate, or Jordyn Tyson over a good prospect on defense, even if he slips. And if Arizona picks Love, you essentially get a free roll with Reese, assuming the Titans don’t trade the pick. Worth a shot.” – Mark Ringo ( Sleepers and Busts ) Carnell Tate drafted in Top 7 ( +105 ) “Carnell Tate’s draft position u7.5 ( +105 at DraftKings ). I’m surprised this bet hasn’t been steamed, but it could be by the time you read this. I’ll grab this bet and take it anywhere I can find it for plus money. Tate’s floor right now looks like seventh overall to the Commanders, and I wouldn’t be shocked if he went as high as fourth overall to the Titans.” – Derek Brown ( FantasyPros ) Fewer than 8.5 SEC players drafted in First Round ( -185 ) “You’ll make money if you bet that there will be fewer than 8.5 players from SEC schools selected in the first round (-185). Normally, the first round of the draft is littered with SEC guys. Not this year. Mansoor Delane (LSU), Kadyn Proctor (Alabama), and Keldric Faulk (Auburn) are the SEC’s only first-round locks, and K.C. Concepcion (Texas A&M) is a near-lock. That’s four. Jermod McCoy (Tennessee), Colton Hood (Tennessee), and Ty Simpson (Alabama) are better than 50/50 to go in the first round, but McCoy’s stock is plummeting due to a worrisome knee issue, and there are only two or three potential first-round suitors for Simpson, none of whom would draft him with the picks they currently hold in the top half of the round. If all of these SEC maybes make it, that’s seven, leaving one SEC player to spare. Chase Bisontis (Texas A&M), Cashius Howell (Texas A&M), Zion Young (Missouri), C.J. Allen (Georgia, and Caleb Banks (Florida) are first-round possibilities. There’s a decent chance one of these players makes it into the first round. I don’t think we’ll see two or more players from this group make it, and if we do get more than one, it could very well be at the expense of McCoy, Hood, or Simpson.” – Pat Fitzmaurice ( FantasyPros ) Carnell Tate to be first WR drafted ( -180 ) “Carnell Tate is the betting favorite to be the first wide receiver selected in the 2026 NFL Draft at -180 odds, largely due to his exceptional route running and ‘pro-ready’ profile. While Jordyn Tyson is hands down the best pure receiver in this class, his extensive injury history, including major knee surgery and a broken collarbone, has dropped him to the second or third receiver off the board on most teams’ lists. NFL front offices are notoriously risk-averse in the top ten, making Tate the safer bet to anchor a professional offense immediately. This shift in draft stock highlights a classic case where reliability outweighs elite but fragile potential. Ultimately, taking Tate at these odds is a play on the certainty of his health and polished Buckeye pedigree over the medical gamble Tyson presents.” – Lawrence Iacona ( Gridiron Experts ) Makai Lemon to be first WR drafted ( +2000 ) “Makai Lemon – 1st Wide Receiver Drafted ( +2000 at Caesars ). I'm going with Makai Lemon as the first wide receiver off the board. Bold, absolutely. Crazy? Maybe, but hear me out. This is often a copycat league. I believe a wide receiver-needy team, such as the New York Giants, might consider Lemon. The Giants already have Malik Nabers, a top outside threat, and could look to replicate what Seattle did with Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Detroit with Amon-Ra St. Brown, using Lemon in a similar role. I'm going with the Giants selecting Lemon at 5, assuming Jeremiyah Love is already off the board.” – Paul Brenton ( EPB1983Dynasty ) Related articles NBA Picks & Predictions: Friday (11/27) NFL Black Friday Same Game Parlays & Picks: Broncos vs. Steelers NFL Black Friday Picks & Predictions: Broncos vs. Steelers NFL Black Friday Anytime & First TD Scorers: Broncos vs. Steelers NFL Black Friday Player Props & Picks: Broncos vs. Steelers College Football Picks & Predictions: Week 13 (Friday) Click to go to homepage NFL Home Odds Picks Matchups Tools Research Articles Teams Leaderboards NBA Home Odds Picks Matchups Tools Research Articles Teams Leaderboards NCAAF Home Odds Picks Matchups Tools Leaderboards Articles Teams Podcast Careers Product Updates BettingPros API Get Involved About Us Contact Us Terms of Use Privacy Policy Third Party Licenses Do Not Sell Accessibility Disclosures Affiliate Signup © 2018–2026 BettingPros.com. He analyzes football on and off the field like no one else on the planet, writing about in-season X's and O's, offseason transactions and so much more. He is the host of the Bill Barnwell Show podcast , with episodes released weekly. Barnwell joined ESPN in 2011 as a staff writer at Grantland. Follow on X Multiple Authors Email Print Open Extended Reactions Thanksgiving week is the start of the sprint to the end of the NFL's regular season . And while there are players who know their teams don't have much to play for between now and then, there are plenty more who have quite a bit riding on what happens over the rest of the 2026 campaign. Those stakes can be different things. For some, it's money, especially for young players on rookie deals who haven't yet signed a potentially lucrative second contract. For others, it's opportunity. There are rotational players who want to establish themselves as starters and veterans hanging on who want to stick in the starting lineup for another season. Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show' I'll take a look at 11 of those players who have the most to gain or lose over the remainder of the season, inspired by what they did in Week 11 and what's to come over the rest of the year. Jump to: Cousins | Metcalf | Pickens McCarthy | Lassiter | Rice Branch | Shough | Andrews Watson | Van Ness Kirk Cousins , QB, Minnesota Vikings Well, the honeymoon is over. Last week, Vikings fans who had witnessed two months of Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz struggling to move the ball welcomed Cousins back with open arms, and despite a few hiccups, the good outweighed the bad. Cousins threw for 207 yards and two touchdowns in a comfortable victory over the rival Packers . On Sunday in what amounted to a de facto home game for the 49ers in Mexico City, the magic dissipated. A great outing from Cousins likely wouldn't have made the difference on a day when the vaunted Vikings defense allowed the 49ers to score touchdowns on three of their first four drives in a 35-10 loss , but coach Kevin O'Connell might have hoped to find out. Cousins went 26-of-38 for 235 yards with a brutal pick-six on an underneath pass that Ji'Ayir Brown jumped and returned to the house without even needing to break stride. After a touchdown on their second drive of the game and a field goal on their third, the Vikings didn't score again the rest of the way, with Justin Jefferson losing a fumble and two fourth-quarter drives failing on downs. Cousins bears the brunt of the blame for the interception, and I suspect he'll wish he played better. But the most notable clip of this game from a Vikings perspective will probably be Cousins shouting at his offensive linemen on the sideline; he was knocked down seven times in the loss. And the issues that plagued Minnesota during the collective stints of Murray and Wentz at quarterback are likely to create problems for it against good teams moving forward. Again, they couldn't run the ball. Aaron Jones Sr . had a physically impressive finish to his touchdown run, but the Vikings turned 21 carries into 69 yards and five first downs. Jordan Mason had a 16-yard carry, but it came against San Francisco's backups in the fourth quarter with Wentz on the field. The run game was mostly hopeless with Cousins out there. An absent run game and a trailing game script takes Cousins away from play-action, which is where he has been at his best as a pro, 2026 included. The Raiders couldn't run the ball, either, but Klint Kubiak is excellent at creating throws for his quarterback with play-fakes, run game be damned. Before his trade to the Vikings , Cousins was third in the NFL in QBR when using play-action and 14th in the league when he was dropping back as a pure passer. Seven of Cousins' eight interceptions with the Raiders came in those pure dropback situations. On Sunday, Cousins was effective using play-action, going 7-of-12 for 91 yards, averaging 7.6 yards per throw. Without it? He went 19-of-26 for 144 yards, averaging 5.5 yards per attempt. That included the pick-six, too. With nothing threatening Brown downfield or any sort of run fake to throw off his read, the 49ers safety was able to come from the backside of the play and poach Cousins' attempted slant to Brown, all but deciding the contest late in the first half. Cousins has made more than $333 million in his career and has a minimum of another $10 million on the way in 2027. While many players on this list might have significant money riding on their performance over the rest of this season, that's probably not as important for Cousins. What might matter, though, is opportunity. If Cousins thrives in his second stint with the Vikings, O'Connell & Co. will likely bring him back as their starter in 2027, especially given the regrets the organization has about letting everyone from Cousins to Sam Darnold to Daniel Jones (and now potentially J.J. McCarthy ) walk out the door in years past. And even if the Vikings decide to go in a different direction, a successful second half from Cousins likely would earn the 38-year-old a starting opportunity somewhere else next season. There's still plenty of time for Cousins to get things right, and there won't be many teams capable of getting a multi-touchdown lead on Brian Flores' defense over the rest of the season. After mostly unbridled enthusiasm from all sides about Cousins returning to the Vikings, though, the blowout loss was the coming-back-to-Earth moment for everyone involved. DK Metcalf , WR, Pittsburgh Steelers George Pickens , WR, Dallas Cowboys Let's start with two wideouts who were essentially part of a multi-deal trade of sorts. The Steelers didn't want to re-sign Pickens, who was one year from unrestricted free agency, and traded him to the Cowboys in 2025 for a third-round pick. That third-rounder became Drew Allar , who is playing behind Aaron Rodgers at quarterback. The Steelers filled their need for a top wideout by sending a second-rounder to the Seahawks for Metcalf. The Seahawks used that pick to move up and select a cornerstone safety in Nick Emmanwori . This sure looks like a three-team trade where two teams won and the Steelers lost. And it's not ideal to see your top wideout finish the day with as many receiving yards as personal foul penalties, but that was the Steelers' situation Sunday. In a frustrating loss to the Eagles , Metcalf caught just one pass on four targets for 2 yards before being ejected late in the third quarter for attempting to poke cornerback Cooper DeJean in the eye. Rodgers dropped back 53 times and was sacked five times, but he spent most of the day targeting rookies Germie Bernard and Max Hurleman . This was probably rock-bottom for Metcalf's very disappointing tenure in Pittsburgh. In addition to trading that second-round pick to the Seahawks for Metcalf, the Steelers gave their new wideout a four-year, $132 million extension. (Emmanwori will make less than $12 million combined over his four-year deal in Seattle.) Metcalf racked up a career-low 850 yards in his first season with the Steelers before a late-season suspension after getting into an altercation with a fan ; he had just two catches in last season's playoff loss to the Texans . Though Rodgers was optimistic about the blossoming connection with his training camp roommate this summer, Metcalf has looked even more detached from the offense this season. He's on pace to finish with just 738 receiving yards and three touchdowns, both of which would be career lows. His 1.3 yards per route run is also a career low, down from his 1.9 YPRR in Seattle and 1.8 YPRR a year ago. At his best, Metcalf has shown the ability to win downfield and overwhelm smaller defensive backs in contested-catch situations. Rodgers didn't make that throw very often in 2025, as Metcalf was targeted just 14 times on deep shots all season. Seven of those throws came in two games, suggesting that the Steelers had it as a priority heading into the game a couple of times and then forgot about getting Metcalf the football for multiple weeks. With Mike McCarthy in the fold in 2026, Rodgers has targeted Metcalf downfield more often, but it hasn't been effective. Metcalf has just five catches on 22 deep shots this season, and that is nearly half of the league's completion rate (39.2%) on those throws. On Sunday, Metcalf was blanketed on both of his deep shots, which occurred with the Steelers on the cusp of the red zone, by star Eagles cornerback Quinyon Mitchell . It didn't matter much in a Steelers blowout, but it was one of the worst reps of the year for the Pittsburgh offense, a unit not known for its aesthetic beauty. If we assume Allar (or another inexperienced quarterback) takes over for Rodgers after the season, you could argue that the Steelers should want to surround their new quarterback with as many useful playmakers as possible. With Rico Dowdle and Jaylen Warren at running back, Bernard and Michael Pittman Jr . at wide receiver, and Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington at tight end, the Steelers should have a solid starting group of backs and pass catchers to go with a young, promising offensive line. In the world the Steelers imagined when they traded for the two-time Pro Bowl wideout, Metcalf would be the No. 1 receiver who puts all of those pieces into favorable roles as secondary and tertiary options. But in this world, he is playing like a very expensive second or third wideout. And crucially, he's owed $26.5 million in cash next year, none of which is guaranteed. Though Metcalf would appeal to teams as a potential cap casualty, it's tough to imagine the veteran wideout receiving that sort of salary if he hits free agency. Getting back to even his 2025 level of play might be enough to earn Metcalf another season on this contract, either from the Steelers or with a trade to another organization. It seems like a fresh start might be the best thing for all involved. A fresh start helped kick Pickens' career into high gear, as the mercurial wideout produced a career year in 2025 after leaving the Steelers to join a pass-happy offense in Dallas. And though he was briefly benched for a game last year after missing the team's bus, he has generally been on the straight and narrow after joining the Cowboys. Though Metcalf was ejected from the loss to the Eagles, Pickens racked up seven catches for 102 yards and a touchdown in a 51-30 win over the Titans . It's admittedly a little easier to score on a bereft Titans defense, but since the start of 2025, Pickens is 13th among wideouts in yards per route run and eighth in ESPN's receiver score . He was a massive bargain for the Cowboys last season, when Pickens made $3.7 million in the final year of his rookie deal. He has lived up to expectations on the franchise tag in 2026, too, making $27.3 million. A second franchise tag for Pickens in 2027 would pay the 25-year-old $32.8 million, which could still be reasonable, considering the top of the wide receiver market is averaging north of $42 million per year. For the Cowboys, though, that might be difficult to justify given how much they're paying the other key players on their roster. Dak Prescott , Quinnen Williams and CeeDee Lamb are already making nearly $130 million per year combined on their three contracts. With Jerry Jones dreaming of a competent defense, would the Cowboys really budget another $33 million to their offense without securing a long-term commitment? Pickens might be the rare legit No. 1 wideout in his prime to hit unrestricted free agency. And though there might have been teams eager to commit to Pickens a year ago after one significant season, a second Pro Bowl-caliber campaign might encourage previously skeptical organizations to make a more substantial investment. Pickens, who has 247 receiving yards and four touchdowns over the past two weeks, can go a long way to locking up that massive deal by keeping this up over the rest of the season. J.J. McCarthy , QB, New York Giants It has gone better than I think anyone could have hoped. After trading for McCarthy in late September, the Giants gave him time in the second half of a loss to the Saints , with McCarthy throwing for 243 yards in what was mostly garbage time. That was enough to earn McCarthy the starting job for the following week's game against the Texans . McCarthy won that game and has gone 3-1 as the starter, coming within a first down or two against the Commanders to begin his Giants career 4-0. After four starts, McCarthy has been solid under center. His 62.8 Total QBR since entering the lineup ranks 14th in the league. He has averaged 8.8 yards per attempt over that span while attacking teams downfield, averaging more than 10 air yards per throw, the most of any quarterback in the league. After committing numerous negative plays for most of his time as the Vikings starter, McCarthy has toned down those problems so far with the Giants. His sack rate is still worse than league average at 7.0%, but that's down from 10% during his lone healthy-ish season in Minnesota. McCarthy has thrown only two interceptions in five games, and though he's lucky to have gotten away with at least one or two would-be picks that weren't caught, he has done a better job of protecting the football with the Giants so far. Sunday was almost the polar opposite of the sort of game McCarthy has played over the previous month. Facing a Jaguars team that created consistent pressure, McCarthy didn't create much as a passer, but he kept the Giants alive by avoiding negative plays. Though he averaged only 4.6 yards per throw, he didn't throw any interceptions and was sacked only once. He ran four times for 38 yards, including a 22-yard scramble that set up a Malik Nabers touchdown. Another long McCarthy scramble was called back for holding on a day when the referees seemed to dominate the proceedings. I'm not sure we've learned whether McCarthy will become a great quarterback. The sack rate is still too high. He's inconsistent and still struggles with his accuracy; he has a below-average completion percentage over expectation (CPOE) despite a better-than-expected drop rate, per NFL Next Gen Stats. The deep-passing emphasis is at least partially a product of the Giants structuring the offense to keep McCarthy from putting the ball in danger. After a month, though, it is clear that he's at least qualified to be on an NFL roster, something that didn't seem to be the case after his disastrous 2025 season in Minnesota. And that will create a very interesting quandary for McCarthy and the Giants. Trading for McCarthy was a logical move for the Giants, who had hopes of competing this year, and at 6-3-1, they've been vindicated for that choice. Even if the Giants miss the postseason, shipping a fifth-round pick will look like a smart move for general manager Joe Schoen. What happens when Jaxson Dart is healthy? The Giants are likely more committed to their 2025 first-round pick than to McCarthy, who won't want to spend the rest of his rookie contract sitting behind Dart. After this season, the Giants also have to decide whether to pick up McCarthy's fifth-year option, which would guarantee the 23-year-old $25.7 million in 2028. Both quarterbacks have flaws, and given their history, both are pretty significant injury risks. The simplest solution might be a competition next offseason, but McCarthy should have some ability to influence the proceedings. If McCarthy continues to play well and the Giants continue to win, it'll be tough to take the job from the new starter. If the Giants really are committed to Dart and see him as a franchise quarterback in 2027, McCarthy would suddenly have some more significant trade value for teams that might see him as a starter in the short- or long-term. Kamari Lassiter , CB, Houston Texans Lassiter entered 2026 as one of the finer young cornerbacks in the NFL. Coming off a Pro Bowl appearance in his second season, Lassiter had earned a reputation as a solid cover cornerback who made a significant contribution with his physicality and tackling. He started Week 1 against the Bills by coming up with a fourth-down stop on Josh Allen on a designed run. And when Allen tossed up a prayer into coverage with 1:48 to go, Lassiter settled under what should have been the game-ending interception. But he dropped it. On the next play, Lassiter allowed the winning touchdown on a deep post to Joshua Palmer . I'm not sure Lassiter has really recovered from it. He has looked overwhelmed by teams that have challenged him vertically, with George Pickens, Parker Washington and Malik Nabers beating him downfield for big plays this season. The Texans moved Lassiter into the slot without much luck. He has also committed nine penalties for 95 yards, including three pass interference calls. Lassiter had just 10 penalties over his first two years combined. His struggles might be a microcosm of the broader and stunning decline of the Texans' defense, which came into the season with a reputation as one of the best in football. The issues extend beyond Lassiter. The defense hasn't exerted the same level of physicality. It has made sloppy mistakes with tackling, and players have taken poor angles to ball carriers. Even as recently as the Week 10 loss to the Browns , the Texans' coverage defenders repeatedly lined up at the same depth in the secondary, allowing a Cleveland offense that relies heavily on rub routes to create easy picks for completions and big plays. The Texans rank 15th in the league in points allowed per drive after 11 weeks, taking a step forward during Thursday's 26-3 victory over the hapless Colts , who cut starting quarterback Daniel Jones after the game. Naturally, Houston hopes this will finally be the game that gets the defense back on track as the 4-6 team tries to sneak into the postseason. Lassiter would obviously play a significant role in that defensive rebirth. And as a cornerback who is about to become eligible for an extension after he completes his third year as a pro, a turnaround might inspire the Texans to give him a new deal. Lassiter seemed on track to get there heading into Year 3, but he'll need to turn things around to earn that deal this offseason. Rashee Rice , WR, Kansas City Chiefs If we only considered Rice's on-field production, he would profile as one of the more exciting pending free agents in next year's class. The 26-year-old has averaged 2.5 yards per route run since entering the league, which would rank ninth in the NFL between Amon-Ra St. Brown and Justin Jefferson if Rice had run enough routes to qualify. He's a force once he has the ball, averaging 7.8 yards after catch, tied with Khalil Shakir for the most of any player in the league. Rice's 67 YAC score in ESPN's receiver scores is fifth best since the start of 2023. Rice might not have the downfield speed and separation to serve as a true No. 1 wide receiver, but Sunday's win over the Cardinals was a good example of how he can be a very useful part of an offense. In 20 routes, he had six catches, five first downs and 53 yards. Rice was really good at shielding the ball from defensive backs on a pair of potentially vulnerable catches and created yards after bringing in the football. It can feel as if Rice indulges the worst parts of Andy Reid's affinity for dinking-and-dunking and slowly working down the field, but he's a valuable high-floor receiver in the Chiefs' offense. The issue with Rice, of course, is availability. He has missed significant time because of a concussion and hamstring and knee injuries in his pro career. Rice was suspended for six games in 2025 after violating the league's personal conduct policy, then went to jail for 30 days last offseason for violating the terms of his probation. He has missed 28 of 68 possible games with the Chiefs over his three-plus years in the NFL so far. Given those circumstances, it's probably not a surprise that the Chiefs have yet to negotiate an extension with Rice, who is a few months from unrestricted free agency. As I wrote about after the Josh Downs trade , I wouldn't be shocked if the Chiefs lean toward giving an extension to their newly acquired wideout instead of re-signing Rice, given the latter's availability issues and off-field concerns. There might not be significant interest around the league in paying Rice, but if he plays great down the stretch and into a deep postseason run for the Chiefs, that might change. Brian Branch , S, Detroit Lions If it weren't for a torn right Achilles , Branch might already be one of the highest-paid safeties in football. Instead, in the middle of his third year as a pro, that Achilles tear ended Branch's 2025 season and made it impossible for him and the Lions to come to terms on an extension that would have pleased both parties. With so many other talented young players due for extensions over the past 18 months in Detroit, Branch's deal fell by the wayside. Now, with edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson and linebacker Jack Campbell on injured reserve, a secondary that struggled badly to begin the year needs to step up for Detroit. It has looked like a different unit from the moment Branch returned to the lineup. Without him on the field this season, the Lions have allowed a 74.0 Total QBR, the third-worst mark in the league. On 152 dropbacks with Branch in the lineup, that figure drops to 32.0, which would be the best in the league over the full season. to know." data-hyperlink="https://www.espn.com/nfl/super-bowl/" data-cta-link-text="Super Bowl Index"> Branch might not single-handedly turn one of the league's worst pass defenses into its best over the rest of the season, but his presence makes life much easier for the rest of the Lions' secondary. Branch is a more reliable and rangier deep safety than the replacement-level options Detroit had for most of the season, and that helps to stop the big plays that plagued the Lions early on. And though he's not a great cover defender, he's at least capable and competitive in the slot and over the middle of the field. Branch's impact is most felt through his physicality. Bucky Irving will be feeling it for a few days, as Branch leveled Irving after a short catch out of the backfield Sunday, briefly knocking the star Bucs running back out of the game. Branch was essentially playing linebacker on that snap, a role he'll fill more often with Campbell out. Per Next Gen Stats, Branch lined up as a deep safety on only 16% of his snaps in Sunday's win over the Buccaneers . Kerby Joseph , who was filling that role, came back from a serious knee injury to play 39 defensive snaps in his first action in more than a year. Before both were injured, Branch and Joseph were the best safety duo in football. As the Lions battle injuries in their front seven and consider what their future looks like on defense, keeping Branch and Joseph together for many years has to appeal to general manager Brad Holmes. As a second-round pick in the 2023 draft, Branch is about to be a free agent. With the safety franchise tag projected to come in at $22.2 million , the Lions might see tagging him as a logical way to continue their relationship while they negotiate a long-term extension. If Branch plays well enough over the next two months, that longer-term deal might be on the table sooner rather than later. Tyler Shough , QB, New Orleans Saints After taking over for Spencer Rattler in the second half of 2025, Shough showed enough in his nine starts as a rookie to keep the starting job. The Saints didn't pursue quarterback options during the offseason and attempted to upgrade the infrastructure around Shough by signing guard David Edwards and using their first-round pick on Arizona State wideout Jordyn Tyson . Though Tyson missed the first half of the year because of a right hamstring issue , Shough shined late in games during September, nearly leading a dramatic comeback against the Lions before pulling one off the following week against the Ravens . Through the first month of the season, Shough was 19th in Total QBR during the first three quarters of games. He has been slightly better over the ensuing two months, ranking 15th by the same metric. In the fourth quarter, Shough was the league's sixth-best QBR in September but has ranked 25th in the final quarter since then. He's averaging just 5.1 yards per attempt in the fourth quarter and a mere 5.8 yards per attempt overall during his past six games, the latter figure ahead of only Tanner McKee and Daniel Jones , who both are no longer starters. McKee is the only quarterback who has averaged fewer yards per completion over that span. Consistency is Shough's issue. He's capable of making great throws and has excellent ball placement, but he also has a habit of struggling with his timing when asked to read out more complicated concepts, coming off potential throws too early or too late. Kellen Moore's offense has leaned on the quick game to make life easier for his young quarterback, and the Saints went with an unusually heavy dose of play-action early against the Bears on Sunday, but Shough still needs to grow as a dropback passer. Shough arguably hasn't had the help he would have needed. The Saints have been dismal running the football this season, ranking 31st in success rate and last in explosive play rate on designed rush attempts. Shough didn't have Tyson or left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr . for two months, and new lead back Travis Etienne Jr . was sidelined for five games because of a left hamstring issue . In an ideal world, all of those pieces would have been in place for the entire season. Well, on Sunday, Banks and Tyson were back on the field. The Saints still weren't efficient running the football, but their running backs averaged more than 5 yards per carry, buoyed by a 46-yard run by Etienne on a toss. Shough added a 30-yard scramble just before halftime to set up a long field goal by Charlie Smyth . The Bears have a solid defense, but this should have been a spot where Shough had enough to move the ball. Instead, he averaged 5.2 yards per pass attempt and was sacked six times, including a safety in the fourth quarter. Four of those six sacks were Shough's fault, either on reps when he didn't throw to an open receiver, held the ball too long or scrambled into a sack. It didn't seem as though he always trusted what he was seeing unless (or until) it was open. That's a dangerous way to play quarterback, and it's one of the specific ways that Caleb Williams has grown over the past two years under Ben Johnson. When you can't run the ball, and you aren't picking up significant yardage as a passer when you do complete throws, you have to be consistent on extended drives to score. The average Saints touchdown drive this season has required nine plays, the third-longest figure in the NFL. Shough doesn't have that sort of consistency yet as a passer. And that win over the Ravens in Week 2 was the only time this year that the Saints have gone all game without committing a turnover. Shough is already 27 years old. (I still don't understand how he is the same age as Jerry Jeudy , who feels like he has been in the league since the late-1990s.) The hope was that Shough's experience in different schemes would allow him to adapt quickly, and a year ago, it looked like he did. Now, it's fair to wonder whether he can grow into something more than a point guard in Moore's offense. Shough will need to show a higher ceiling over the second half of the season to keep the Saints from pursuing quarterbacks more aggressively next offseason. Mark Andrews , TE, Baltimore Ravens The Ravens made a mistake. Last year, with both Andrews and Isaiah Likely approaching free agency, general manager Eric DeCosta chose the veteran in the tight end room. He signed Andrews to a three-year, $39 million extension in December. Likely left for the Giants in free agency, signing a three-year, $40 million deal to join John Harbaugh in North Jersey. You get a feeling that the number being $1 million more might have mattered just a tiny bit during those negotiations. Deshaun Watson , QB, Cleveland Browns Watson's Browns were on bye this week, but with the Ravens and Steelers both losing, the Browns' chances of making an unexpected trip to the postseason improved. Lukas Van Ness , Edge, Green Bay Packers Van Ness is a 2023 first-round pick who has flashed in years past. He's currently 25th in the league in pass rush win rate on the edge, succeeding just under 20% of the time. He has generated quick pressures 8.6% of the time, per NFL Next Gen Stats. That's good for the fourth-best mark in the league among defenders with at least 200 pass-rush opportunities so far this season. Gutekunst has already made a serious commitment to Parsons, but there are plenty of teams that find it in their budgets to pay two great edge rushers. The Packers feel confident that they have one in Parsons, who is expected to make his debut against the Rams on Wednesday .
