Yet, Warren is projected for 25.5 yards and 3.5 receptions, whereas Dowdle is at 13.5 and 2.5. Given how willingly Aaron Rodgers targets the backs and how poor the Bengals' linebackers are in coverage and at tackling in the open field, backfield receiving production should be a strong part of Pittsburgh's offensive approach, and Dowdle is the far cheaper option in what should be near a 50/50 opportunity split. Keep an eye on this number live. If Warren starts out the first quarter taking most of the snaps on a couple of Pittsburgh three-and-outs, Dowdle's numbers will drop even more, and I'll start looking for live alts. Tutu Atwell receiving yards OVER 30.5 (-109) It's worth wondering just who it is that is going to catch passes for the Los Angeles Rams . Star wide receiver Puka Nacua -- who had 19 targets and 14 receptions on 43 routes last week against the Commanders -- joins Davante Adams and Jordan Whittington on the injured reserve bench. Tight end Terrance Ferguson is also probably out for Sunday's game at Arizona. The two primary route runners behind Nacua at receiver last Sunday were Konata Mumpfield and Atwell, the latter of whom was targeted five times for two receptions and 16 yards. Atwell ended the day with 37 unrealized air yards -- that is to say, he had 53 air yards to the 16 receiving yards he actually produced. In back-to-back weeks, he has had at least 50 air yards on 17 and 20 routes, respectively. Given the thinness of the Rams' receiver room, 20 routes should be a floor projection for Atwell, as long as the Cardinals' offense can keep things competitive with Carson Beck under center. Even if they can't, Atwell's downfield usage can get us home on one big reception. If you're looking to get really frisky in what should be a sleepy late afternoon game, Rams rookie receiver CJ Daniels to score a touchdown is +950. He's a big-framed receiver, which the Rams will need behind the smaller Mumpfield and Atwell. Worth a sprinkle! Tre Tucker receiving yards OVER 25.5 (-115) NFL Pick 'Em FREE to play. Create up to 10 entries and compete for 58 prizes worth $102K. Make Your Picks Speaking of unrealized air yards, Tucker is 13th among all receivers in unconnected air yards at 227. Tucker is tied for ninth in targets of at least 20 air yards but has only a 35.7% receptions rate, thanks in large part to six of those 14 targets landing inaccurate with quarterback Kirk Cousins . Cousins, for as good as he was at the helm of the Raiders' offense, lacks a deep-ball arm at this stage of his career. With rookie Fernando Mendoza ready to start his first career game, I expect the Raiders' passing attack to become less incremental and a bit more vertical, which speaks to Tucker's game. Though the matchup against the Seattle Seahawks ' defense is certainly an intimidating one for a green passer, Klint Kubiak is well suited to find space against this defense -- he saw it work for a whole season up close when he was the coordinator in Seattle last season. I'm confident he'll have a trick or two up his sleeve. I wouldn't usually take a receiving over against this Seahawks defense that leads the league in yards per target allowed to opposing wideouts. But the number is too low for a primary receiver and can be reached on one big play. I'll be on alts as well for this bet, and we also will track 40-plus yards for a half unit at +194. Geno Smith passing yards OVER 220.5 (-113) The Buffalo Bills ' defense has enjoyed two softer quarterback matchups after their bye. Against the Ravens, both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley went down, forcing emergency third quarterback Joe Fagnano into the game. Against the Vikings, it was backup Carson Wentz . Perhaps something seriously improved in the Bills' secondary post-bye -- and they are adding safety Amani Hooker , a nice deadline addition, at safety -- but before that bye, opposing quarterbacks were ripping through Buffalo's pass defense. Cousins had 313 yards in Week 6, Matthew Stafford had 383 in Week 5, and Drake Maye had 269 in Week 4. The Bills are rightfully large favorites over the 2-7 New York Jets , who probably will run the ball early in an attempt to keep it close, then eventually get forced into a pass-heavy script. Smith has cleared this number in three of his past four games and is 11th in the league in yards per pass attempt. When the Jets have to throw, he puts up big numbers. With Garrett Wilson expected to return from the concussion protocol, the Jets' receiver trio is at full force, and Smith should produce accordingly. Check out the latest Super Bowl odds and major NFL awards futures . Daniel Jones passing yards UNDER 186.5 (-112) The Indianapolis Colts receiver room is as bad as any I can think of in the past 10 years of non-COVID football. With Downs and Keenan Allen both traded at the deadline, the Colts are fielding Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin and Deion Burks as starting wideouts. Indianapolis retained running back Jonathan Taylor at the trade deadline, so it's fair to expect the Colts to increase their reliance on the handoff game. The Miami Dolphins ' passing defense gives up the third-most yards per pass attempt in the league but gives up only 198.4 yards per game, right around league average. That's because nobody needs to throw it against them to win. Especially with defensive tackle Zach Sieler now hurt, the Colts should be able to run the ball with plenty of success. This Colts' passing attack is as below league average as it gets, and with Malik Willis out, the likelihood the Dolphins get a second-half lead and force a pass-happy approach is greatly diminished. Is the Colts' defense good? It is not. But it almost doesn't matter. Indianapolis is a 3.5-point favorite, and the chances of a disastrous mistake from McCord is elevated given his status as a former sixth-round pick who has never taken a pro snap in a regular-season game. My model, which is making those quite negative assumptions about McCord, prices this at +450. New England Patriots to NOT allow a sack on first drive (-391) The Patriots are light underdogs this week against the Detroit Lions , who do boast the second-best pass rush win rate this season. But the Patriots are third best in pass block win rate, which, along with Drake Maye 's average sack rate, is why my model isn't overly concerned about Maye falling to a first-drive sack. At least not at this price, anyway. I make the fair line -514. Chase Young under 0.75 sacks (+158) Believe it or not Young is tied for second in the NFL in sacks with 8.0 (only behind Will Anderson Jr .) and this line is absolutely a reflection of that. I generally consider myself a Chase Young backer -- because after the early disappointment of his career he quickly became underrated - but wow has this gone too far. In fact, if the line closes at this price it would be the strongest sack prop line of the year. There is no way Young - whose pass rush win rate is above average but still just in the 69th percentile - is on that kind of level. Chop Robinson over 0.25 sacks (+132) This will be the fifth time I've bet Robinson's sack over in this year's column and it doesn't look like we'll be slowing down any time soon (we're 2-2 and +1.1 units thus far). Robinson is the league leader in pass rush win rate at edge. Let me say that again: he is the league leader in pass rush win rate at edge. And to back it up: he leads edge rushers in pressure rate, too! That's multiple forms of measurement coming away with the same conclusion: on a down-to-down basis Robinson is consistently beating his blocker and causing problems for the quarterback. That it's only resulted in 4.0 sacks is why we still get to bet it at this price. And this week, we get an added bonus: the Dolphins aren't even that big underdogs this week (+4.5 at the Colts). Two years ago he recorded a tackle rate on run plays that ranked in the 94th percentile among interior linemen with at least 300 snaps played, along with a 97th percentile run stop win rate. But he is not the same player now at age 33. Among defensive tackles with 200 snaps plays this year Stewart ranks in the 63rd percentile in tackle rate against the run and the 12th percentile in run stop win rate. Even against the run-heavy Dolphins my model believes this line is a little too optimistic for Stewart. Bryan Cook under 6.5 tackles + assists (-149) This is an increased line from where Cook has been in the past couple of weeks after he went over this number twice in the last three games (though those are the only two times he's gone over this line all year). Only 29% of tackle lines on safeties this year have been 6.5 or higher, and I'm not sure Cook ought to be quite on that level even with this number shaded under. Cook ranks in the 82nd percentile in tackle rate vs. the pass but just 38th percentile against the run, but those equate to nearly equal tackling rates so I don't think game script is a huge factor here. Overall, my model thinks this line is a little high. Running backs record a reception on 8% dropbacks against man coverage but 15% against zone. And based on back-testing research, I don't believe this fact is fully baked into reception lines. The last couple of weeks I've used this information to bet the under on running backs facing man-heavy defenses -- we hit on Alvin Kamara 's under last week -- but this time I'm flipping the script and opting for Brown's over against the Steelers. Pittsburgh is the heaviest zone coverage team in the NFL, running zone 79% of the time. Malik Washington receiving yards OVER 30.5 (-116) Washington has a huge split between his open score (82, T2) and his catch score (38, below average). Those are two player tracking-based metrics from ESPN Analytics, with the former measuring a receiver's ability to get open (regardless of target) on every route and the latter measuring their ability to make the catch relative to expectations. Open score is much more stable than catch score and correlates more strongly with production, so Washington fits the exact profile of receiver I want to bet on. Yes, he will have McCord throwing to him. But I also think this is a particularly good matchup; Colts nickel corner Justin Walley has been out, but even if he returns, he has had a rough season, giving up 1.8 yards per coverage snap, per NFL Next Gen Stats. That's much higher than average. This bet is based on my read of the number above and not an output from a model, the way most of my bets are. NFL player props are bets on a specific statistical outcome for a specific NFL player. We cover passing yards, rushing yards, receiving yards, and anytime touchdowns in our tool, but there are countless other betting opportunities every week. Every prop bet has two parts: The number (Over or Under 81.5 rushing yards, for example) The price, which determines how much a winning bet returns and reflects the implied probability If two players are lined at 45.5 receiving yards, that does not necessarily mean they have the same implied odds. Player A — Over 45.5 receiving yards (-115) — 53.5% implied over probability — Winning $100 bet has $187 return Player B — Over 45.5 receiving yards (+105) — 48.8% implied over probability — Winning $100 bet has $205 return When Do NFL Player Props Come Out Each Week? Some marquee player props are posted earlier in the week, but the majority are released on Wednesday or Thursday after injury reports have been announced. Top 3 High-Confidence Prop Highlights To narrow the card down to the strongest statistical plays of the week, the three selections below represent the highest confidence ratings from oddsmakers across the entire schedule. Daniel Jones (Colts) – Over 0.5 Passing TDs (-333): At -333 NFL odds , backing Daniel Jones to throw at least one touchdown serves as a highly reliable parlay anchor. The Colts sit as strong 65.8% favorites against the Dolphins. Market confidence overwhelmingly projects Jones to exploit a soft secondary in the red zone, easily clearing this line. Deshaun Watson (Browns) – Under 1.5 Passing TDs (-278): Carrying steep -278 odds, fading Deshaun Watson represents a premier defensive-based trend. The Browns face a relentless Texans pass rush. Analyst picks and parlay prices reflect the lines at which they were quoted. Read all of Andrew Erickson's NFL Week 11 picks and predictions . Jaguars vs. Giants Preview & Picks Erickson's pick: Jacksonville Jaguars -5.5 Trends As a road favorite (the role it plays here), JAX is 2-0 ATS (100%) and 2-0 O/U in 2026 (n=2, through Week 10). Overall: across all road games, 3-1 ATS and 2-2 O/U; across all games as a favorite, 5-2 ATS and 5-2 O/U; across all 2026 games, 6-3 ATS and 5-4 O/U. As a home underdog (the role it plays here), NYG is 2-1 ATS (67%) and 2-1 O/U in 2026 (n=3, through Week 10). Overall: across all home games, 3-2 ATS and 3-2 O/U; across all games as an underdog, 4-2 ATS and 4-2 O/U; across all 2026 games, 6-3 ATS and 5-4 O/U. JAX streaks through Week 10: 7-2 straight up (3-game win streak), 6-3 against the spread (3-game cover streak), 5-4 toward the total (4-game Over streak). NYG streaks through Week 10: 5-3-1 straight up (1-game losing streak), 6-3 against the spread (1-game non-cover streak), 5-4 toward the total (1-game Over streak; NYG has gone Over in five of its last six games). JAX comes in off a 40-23 road win at TEN as a 10.5-point favorite, covering (Week 10). NYG comes in off a 24-21 home loss to WAS as a 1.5-point favorite, failing to cover (Week 10; TNF). NYG has 3 more days of rest than JAX. Teams with at least 3 more days of rest than their opponent are 22-12-1 ATS and 27-8 straight up in 2026 (35 games, through Week 10). Favorites in that spot are 18-5-1 ATS and 23-1 straight up; underdogs in that spot are 4-7 ATS and 4-7 straight up. NYG is the underdog with the rest edge. Home underdogs are 21-36-2 ATS in 2026 (59 games, through Week 10, neutral sites excluded). NYG is a home underdog in this game. Games with closing totals from 45.5 to 49.5 are 25-21 toward the Over in 2026 (46 games, through Week 10), averaging 49.7 combined points against an average closing total of 47.3. Scoring environment in 2026 (combined points per game against the average closing total): JAX 45.9 against 44.1 (5-4 O/U); NYG 44.3 against 43.2 (5-4 O/U). JAX is 4-2 ATS and 4-2 O/U over its last six games (2026 Week 4 through Week 10); NYG is 4-2 ATS and 5-1 O/U over its last six games (2026 Week 4 through Week 10). Jacksonville’s +125 point differential is the best in the NFL through Week 10, and the Jaguars’ five wins by 17 or more points are two more than any other team. Betting Preview The lines look spot-on to me. Jacksonville has benefited from facing compromised offenses and weaker opponents, and the Giants are one of the better teams the Jaguars have faced recently. New York has been competitive in consecutive divisional games and has extra rest after playing Thursday, and Jacksonville is traveling for a second consecutive road game. Still, the Jaguars are 7-2 through nine games for the first time since 1999, when that team went 14-2, and they have a +125 point differential, the best in the NFL and second-best through nine games in franchise history behind the 1999 team’s +137 (Next Gen Stats). And it should be noted that the Giants have played just one team that currently holds a winning record. I like Jacksonville. They are a wagon. Per Next Gen Stats: The Jaguars enter Week 11 as the only team that ranks top five in both points per game (29.9, 4th) and points per game allowed (16.0, 2nd), leading the NFL with a +125 point differential. The Jaguars’ win over Tennessee was their fifth win by 17 or more points this season, two more than any other team, and this will be the first game where the new Jacksonville defensive players are available (Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III). Note that there is rain in the forecast, but my lean is still toward the Over at 46.5 points. Sharps are backing the Over 46.5 total points at -104 (based on $18K in prediction market liquidity). FanDuel offers -104 ( Smart Money Tool ). The Jaguars have covered in seven of their last eight road games (and gone Over in four straight games). Best NFL Same Game Parlay for Jaguars vs. Giants Here is our three-leg same game parlay for Jaguars vs. Giants. View all of our Week 11 NFL same game parlays . Parlay odds courtesy of DraftKings Sportsbook. Leg 1: Cam Skattebo Under 54.5 Rushing Yards ( -111 ) Leg 2: Isaiah Likely Under 49.5 Receiving Yards ( -110 ) Leg 3: Malik Nabers 60+ Receiving Yards ( -152 ) Cam Skattebo and Isaiah Likely have both been very productive lately. Skattebo has 78 and 144 rushing yards in his last two games, while regaining the Giants' lead-back role. Meanwhile, Likely just went off for 127 yards last week. Despite those stat lines, both New York players are worth fading in this week's matchup. The Jaguars have been stout against the run and are defending tight ends at a high level. The defense allows only 67.4 rushing yards per game to opposing running backs, the third-lowest mark in the NFL. The additions of defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux will boost the run defense even more. Jacksonville is also allowing a league-low 31.0 receiving yards per game to tight ends. So, let's take the under on both Skattebo and Likely's yardage props. Likely has 50+ receiving yards in five of his last six games, while Skattebo has 55+ rushing yards in five of his past six games as well. Many of those performances have come against easier competition, though. The Jaguars' defense presents a notable step up in competition for the Giants. Although we're hoping for Skattebo and Likely to be limited, Malik Nabers should be productive. The Jags are giving up the fifth-most receiving yards per game to opposing wideouts. Teams target Jacksonville's secondary, and Nabers could see more targets if the Giants fall behind. Nabers has been quiet lately, with just 44 and 43 yards in the last two games. However, he can wake back up in this matchup. It wasn't that long ago when Nabers went off for 100+ yards in four straight games. We don't need 100+ yards this week, just 60+ to cash our parlay. After favorites wrecked Week 9, the underdogs got out to an early win. I have three early picks for primetime games in Germany, Cincinnati, and Baltimore. Best of luck and enjoy the weekend! Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings . Lions (-2.5) vs Patriots: O/U 51.5 The Lions and Patriots will meet in Munich, Germany, with a potential shootout on our hands. Last week, Green Bay torched New England’s secondary for almost 400 passing yards, and the Patriots face Detroit, which hasn’t had to throw the last two games. Jared Goff has thrown 25 pass attempts in each of his past two games against the Dolphins and Vikings and gone under 200 yards. Goff hasn’t gone under 200 passing yards in back-to-back games since 2024. Before the previous two games, Goff threw at least 30 passes in six straight and 38 or more in three. This is a spot where I think he clears 30 and could approach 40 pass attempts. The Patriots run the second-most man coverage (28.5%), and that opens the door for this Lions offense. Detroit scored 31 on the Jets, and Goff went 25-of-32 for 269 yards and two touchdowns; and that’s important because that’s the only game that Goff has faced against a team ranked top 10 in man coverage rate. The Patriots are obviously a step up from the Jets defensively, and after the New England secondary was trashed by Jordan Love , Christian Watson , and Matthew Golden last week, this prop just seems that much better. I like Goff Over 34.5 pass attempts up to 35.5. The only quarterback who’s gone for 35-plus against New England is Aaron Rodgers (39) , but that’s about to change. I also added Drake Maye to go Over 33.5 pass attempts and Over 1.5 passing touchdowns. Maye is basically the offense at this point and he has a good matchup with Detroit. The fact that A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson are back helps Maye out, but they aren’t 100-percent, and neither is the Pats offensive line (down 2 starters). Maye has thrown two-plus touchdowns in six-straight games and I think that could continue against a Lions defense that allows a lot of explosives through the air. This could be a shoot out and New England is getting desperate. Picks: Jared Goff Over 34.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Drake Maye Over 33.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit), Maye over 1.5 Pass TDs (1 unit) Chiefs (-3) at Falcons: O/U 47.5 No Kenneth Walker opens the door for Patrick Mahomes to have a day. The Falcons’ opponents have the ninth-highest pass rate over exception this season, and it’s third if you remove the Buccaneers game where Baker Mayfield threw three times in a monsoon. Atlanta is allowing 228.0 passing yards per game, but remove that Mayfield performance and the number rises to 271.3, which would rank last in the NFL. Here is the list of quarterbacks and how they’ve performed this season against Atlanta. Joe Burrow: 271 Baker Mayfield: 0 Brock Purdy: 288 Caleb Williams: 305 Tyler Huntley: 201 Tyler Shough: 286 Jordan Love: 312 Bryce Young: 287 Aaron Rodgers: 221 Six out of nine quarterbacks went over 240 passing yards, including three of the last four, and six of the past eight. Mahomes has thrown for at least 240 passing yards in five of eight games and two straight. Emmett Johnson has a surprising rushing prop of 71.5 and a rush + rec prop of 102.5, so he may get a heavy dosage, but in a dome setting, I think Kansas City reverts to trusting Mahomes more. I think he adds another to his resume in Atlanta. I’d go up to 244.5. This prop was 236.5 yesterday. Pick: Patrick Mahomes 240+ Passing Yards (1 unit) Jaguars (-10.5) at Titans: O/U 46.5 I lost on Tony Pollard ‘s under rushing yards last week against the Bengals, but will run it back on his Under. Pollard has 129 and 117 rushing yards in back-to-back games on 25 and 21 carries, plus five touchdowns. Both game scripts worked out that Tennessee was in the game until the final whistle, so running the ball was never out of the question. However, that could change here. Not only could the bye week throw off the ground game’s rhythm, but this matchup is the toughest of the season on paper. In the last three games, Derrick Henry was held to 57 rushing yards last week, and Jonathan Taylor to 23 yards two weeks ago, plus Woody Marks had 56 yards. Jacksonville ranks fifth in the NFL with 89.3 rushing yards allowed per game, but that also dropped after Justice Hill had a garbage-time 65-yard run last week. Pollard has hit the over in three straight games and is 5-3 to the over on the season. I’m buying into regression hitting this week. I’m taking the under 58.5 rushing yards down to 53.5. I expect a negative game script and Pollard’s role in the pass game to increase here, and his carries regress back to the norm. Last season, Pollard ran for 60 and 48 yards against the Jaguars on 10 and 14 carries. Jacksonville won by 22 and 34 points. Pick: Tony Pollard Under 58.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Peacock offers one of the most comprehensive live sports streaming lineups available today, bringing together the NFL, NBA, MLB, WNBA, Premier League, NCAA football, NCAA basketball, golf, motorsports, and major global sporting events in a single service. Vikings at Packers (-3): O/U 42.5 Did you know that Jordan Love is the only quarterback to throw for two touchdowns against the Vikings this season? That was in Week 1, so seven-straight quarterbacks have thrown for one or fewer touchdowns against Minnesota. Well, fast forward to Week 10, and Green Bay still doesn’t have a running game, so Love has carried the offense. If the Packers are to score more than two touchdowns in this game, it’s hard for me to see it not coming from the arm of Love. He is 8-1 to the over 1.5 passing touchdowns this season. I’ll take him to go Over 1.5 passing touchdowns against Minnesota again and ride his heater of three-straight overs. Outside boundary receivers have had a hard time against Minnesota this season, but one wideout that burned the Vikings defense was Matthew Golden . He’s burned me too. I faded Golden the past two weeks, and he snuck over with 79 yards, then had a monster 164 yards against New England. This becomes a fade spot of a career-high and after catching all 10 targets. I am going under 71.5 yards on Golden, down to 66.5. I’ll root for a red zone touchdown from him, though. Picks: Jordan Love Over 1.5 Passing TDs (1 unit), Matthew Golden Under 71.5 Receiving Yards (1 unit) Steelers at Bengals (-3.5): O/U 49.5 It may be November, but this game will feel like a December or January clash with playoff implications. The Steelers and Bengals are both on four-game winning streaks, and the winner will be in first place in the AFC North. The spread and total for this first game were Bengals -3.5 and 42.5, so we have a full seven-point correction on the total for the second game after Pittsburgh won 30-27 in Week 3. Pittsburgh has been money in years past with Mike Tomlin coming off a bye week (17-5 ML), but this Mike McCarthy’s team now, plus the Bengals, are incredible when at a rest disadvantage. Since 2019 with Zac Taylor , the Bengals are 18-5-1 ATS with a rest disadvantage. Rather than picking a side, I am going under 24.5 points in the first half. The first-half score was 17-17 in Week 3 and flew over the 20.5 first-half total. There could be a lack of rhythm early coming out of the break for the Steelers, and it’ll be hard for the Bengals to replicate or improve on their 7.1-yard play last week against Atlanta. Plus, the Bengals are going off an overseas game, which is never easy on the body. With the intensity of this game early, I like the first half under 24.5 points. Neither team has played anybody good while lighting it up during their four-game win streaks, so the defenses may surprise us. Pick: Steelers vs Bengals 1H Under 24.5 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Chargers at Ravens (-4.5): O/U 38.5 If you were the Chargers and had to pick an opponent, you’d be picking from the Colts, Dolphins, Eagles, and Ravens at this point (LA lost to the Raiders and Cardinals). This is as good of a matchup for the Chargers offense as it gets. Baltimore has allowed 33-plus points in three straight games, and it might not get better with questionable tags to three starting defensive backs. This is also the Chargers’ first primetime game of the season and first of two or three (Week 15 could get flexed). I think Los Angeles will want this game a little more, and Jim Harbaugh might call up his brother John for any secrets to pull off the win against his former Ravens team. It doesn’t scare me that Jacoby Brissett will be making his Ravens debut in Baltimore on Monday Night Football, because, like I said, that Ravens’ defense has some serious issues. The Chargers finally found the end zone last week after 37 straight drives without a touchdown, and I think they’ll find it more than once in Baltimore. I like the Chargers to get the first cover of the season (0-7-1 ATS), and I think they can win too. Baltimore is 0-4 ATS at home (worst) and 2-7 ATS this season (third-worst). I will take L.A. +4.5. Now the Vikings get their biggest test yet. Here is how I'm wagering the weekend in the professional football ranks. This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX Sports may be compensated. Read more about Sports Betting on FOX Sports . Vikings vs. 49ers The Vikings are a different team with Kirk Cousins at quarterback. We saw last weekend that average quarterback play can turn a struggling, inept offense into a group that scores like an average NFL offense. It feels easy to take Minnesota again against San Francisco in Mexico City. However, I'm going to skip the side and total in favor of a prop. The 49ers rely on Christian McCaffrey as the workhorse of their offense, and that was on full display last weekend. He had 13 carries for just over 60 yards and added four catches for 161 yards. I'm targeting his receptions number in this game. The Vikings love to pressure the quarterback, and their blitz and pressure rates are among the highest in NFL history. One way to combat that pressure is to get the running back out of the backfield quickly and find him on mismatches. We saw it last week when McCaffrey got matched up on Von Miller for a touchdown. I think the 49ers have to use McCaffrey in the passing game to have success against Minnesota's pressure. I like the Over on his receptions. Schwartz's Pick: Christian McCaffrey Over 4.5 receptions Buccaneers @ Lions This line could reflect Tampa Bay possibly being without quarterback Baker Mayfield, who is questionable with multiple injuries. However, I believe Mayfield will play, with the Bucs still in the hunt for a division title. He's a tough guy, and he won't miss this game. Even still, I'd still take the Bucs with Jalon Daniels under center. This number is too big. Detroit's defense is without its two best players: Jack Campbell is unavailable, and star pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson was injured last week. The Lions' pass rush is significantly worse without Hutchinson, and any team, including the Bucs, will take advantage of it. No Lions lead will be safe moving forward. Tampa Bay has the weapons to score on this defense, and I believe it will. On the other side, there is Detroit's fantastic offense. It's a legitimately good group. However, the Bucs are first in the NFL in defensive EPA per play, even ahead of the Vikings, and they're good at stopping both the run and the pass. They haven't faced an offense quite like the Lions yet, but their defensive production has still been excellent. I believe Tampa Bay's defense can slow down the Lions enough to cover. Mandatory Credit: Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images My early Week 11 NFL player props start with two running backs coming off very different Sundays James Cook broke a 74-yard run for Buffalo, while Christian McCaffrey did most of his damage as a receiver See my three Week 11 NFL prop picks and projected lines below James Cook ran for 157 yards against the Jets. Christian McCaffrey had 161 yards receiving against Dallas. Both performances will draw attention to their Week 11 NFL player props, but I’d approach their rushing totals very differently. Last week, two of my three early targets cleared their projected lines. Jaxon Smith-Njigba had 171 receiving yards and Ja’Marr Chase caught 11 passes. McCaffrey fell three rushing yards short, even as he scored three touchdowns. Cook gets Miami in Buffalo, McCaffrey faces Minnesota in Mexico City and Chase visits Washington on Monday night. Here are the three NFL player props I’m targeting and the opening numbers I’d play. NFL Week 11 Player Props to Target Player Prop Projected Line Christian McCaffrey (SF vs MIN) Under Rushing Yards 74.5 James Cook (BUF vs MIA) Over Rushing Yards 89.5 Ja’Marr Chase (CIN at WAS) Over Receptions 7.5 These are my projected Week 11 lines. When the markets open, compare the number and price across NFL betting apps . NFL Player Prop Pick #1: Christian McCaffrey Rushing Yards Christian McCaffrey’s rushing yards have stayed under 74.5 in eight of nine games. His median is 64 yards. Even his best game, a 75-yard afternoon against Arizona, would have beaten my projected line by just half a yard. McCaffrey has had seven, 18 and 13 carries in his last three games. Las Vegas was the one opponent in that stretch against whom he got a steady afternoon of handoffs. He finished with 68 yards. Dallas gave up 161 receiving yards to McCaffrey on just four catches. I want his rushing under if the line opens in the mid-70s: he can hurt Minnesota on a screen or a wheel route without adding a yard to his rushing total. Minnesota has allowed 4.2 yards per carry on 241 attempts. The workload I’d worry about is 18 or 19 carries. At 13, the number he got in Dallas, he’d need a gain of nearly six yards per attempt to beat me. My cutoff matters here. If the opening line lands near the 62 yards he put up in Dallas, I’d pass. In the mid-70s, I’m happy to let his receiving yards grab the headlines. Early Bet: Christian McCaffrey under 74.5 rushing yards (estimated target) NFL Player Prop Pick #2: James Cook Rushing Yards When I compare rushing yards odds , James Cook is the back I want at 89.5. He’s rushed for at least 90 yards in six of nine games, including five of the six in which Buffalo gave him 20 or more carries. Cook has 344 rushing yards on 70 attempts over his last three games. Two of those afternoons show why I’d play the over against Miami, even if the Dolphins keep him from breaking another long touchdown. 74-YARD TD FOR JAMES COOK BUFvsNYJ on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/DFRLVP17FL — NFL (@NFL) November 15, 2026 Cook’s 74-yard touchdown against the Jets accounted for nearly half of his 157 yards. His other 17 carries went for 83, seven short of what I’m looking for against the Dolphins. The Minnesota game is why I don’t need a repeat of that highlight. Cook’s longest run against the Vikings went for 11 yards. He still finished with 107 because Buffalo went back to him 31 times. Miami has allowed 1,066 rushing yards on 270 attempts, 4.0 per carry, without giving up a run longer than 27 yards in that sample. Teams have kept running on them, which suits how Cook piles up yardage. If Buffalo falls behind and has to throw, the cushion disappears. Cook had just 57 yards on 13 carries in Houston and 75 on 12 against New England. I’m backing him to get closer to his usual workload at home. Early Bet: James Cook over 89.5 rushing yards (estimated target) NFL Player Prop Pick #3: Ja’Marr Chase Receptions For Ja’Marr Chase’s receptions prop against Washington, I’m looking at how quickly Cincinnati’s passing game has shifted. Chase caught 32 passes in his last three games. It took all six of his previous games combined to catch that many. He went for 11 catches against Tennessee, 10 against Atlanta and 11 against Pittsburgh. He’s reached eight in four of nine games overall, so this pick depends on Cincinnati continuing to feed him the way it has over the last three games. The Pittsburgh highlight is the 231 receiving yards. For NFL total receptions props , I give the Atlanta game just as much weight. Chase cleared this target by two catches there without needing anything close to 231 yards. Washington has allowed 217 receptions for 2,341 receiving yards to all positions this season. That total includes backs and tight ends, so it tells us what opponents have done through the air, not which receiver will get the ball. Eight catches is where I’d draw the line for Chase. I’d play the over at 7.5 on Monday night. At 8.5, the price of admission becomes a ninth catch, something Chase managed just once in those first six games. That’s where I’d stop. Follow on X Multiple Authors Sep 25, 2026, 06:39 AM ET Email Print Open Extended Reactions Value is value, no matter where -- or how -- you find it. And that's what we'll aim to do each week in this space: finding betting value. Ben Solak, Seth Walder and Matt Bowen bring different perspectives into how they approach sports betting. Solak leans on his expertise in player evaluation and the X's and O's to find edges, while Walder relies on statistical models to pick out plus-expected value bets, focusing mainly on defense. Bowen, a former NFL safety, predicts positive matchups and game-winners from tape study and his understanding of the league. From spreads and money lines to totals and defensive player props, a good price might be found anywhere. Results will be tracked throughout the season, with flat one-unit wagers for each listed bet. With that, let's dive into our best bets, favorite defensive props and the top game to bet in Week 3. Note: Odds by DraftKings and subject to change. Jump to: Bowen's Game of the Week | Solak's plays | Walder's props Bowen's Game of the Week Kansas City Chiefs at Miami Dolphins (-10.5, 46.5) 1 p.m. ET on CBS, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens, Fla. Travis Kelce is off to a fast start for the Chiefs, who are big favorites Sunday in Miami. Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images I tend to stay away from double-digit spreads in this league (especially for road favorites). That can be bad business given the talent level and coaching we get on Sundays. But looking at the matchup and scheme advantages with Kansas City, I'm in on Andy Reid's team. I'll give you my quick notes for both clubs, along with some player props. NFL betting • Survivor pools: Calm after early storm? • Survivor strategy: Take Jags, Texans • Best bets for Thanksgiving Day games • Odds for Week 12 games | Early bets • Purdy jumps Allen, trails Burrow for MVP • Super Bowl odds: 49ers alone at the top • Betting home | Super Bowl on ESPN When the Chiefs have the ball: The offseason addition of Kenneth Walker III has given the Chiefs a true difference-maker with dual-threat traits in the backfield. Walker has rushed for at least 117 yards -- with at least 23 carries -- in both games this season, and in a Week 2 win over the Indianapolis Colts he caught six of 10 targets for 61 yards. We can expect Walker to get his touches on the ground against a Miami defense giving up 112.5 rushing yards per game (18th in the NFL), which allows Reid's unit to control offensive tempo. In the pass game, I see clear matchup advantages for the Chiefs. The Dolphins are giving up an average of 8.6 YPA (30th in the NFL), and they play man coverage at a rate of 58.9% (fourth most). Look for Reid to set up his receivers for catch-and-run throws from Patrick Mahomes , with Rashee Rice and Travis Kelce working multiple levels of the field against a Miami secondary that lacks high-end talent. When Miami has the ball: The Dolphins have struggled to build offensive rhythm and lack an identity, having failed to score more than 13 points in each of their first two games. Running back De'Von Achane has rushed for a total of 110 yards this season, and we aren't seeing his elite pass-catching ability (he has only 49 yards receiving). Quarterback Malik Willis has shown flashes, but his accuracy has been inconsistent (completing 58% of his passes), and he has thrown only one touchdown pass. Now, Miami does have some young talent in the pass game with Malik Washington , Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell , but Douglas has been ruled out for this matchup after missing practice all week with an ankle injury. The Dolphins lack a proven No. 1 who can win critical game situations at a high rate and they average only 183.5 passing yards per game. Now they'll face a multiple Chiefs defense -- one that leans on late movement and schemed pressure. This Kansas City defense is giving up 90 yards rushing per game and only 5.5 YPA. Miami will need to find a way to create positive game flow while producing some explosive plays to stay in this one. NFL Pick 'Em FREE to play. Create up to 10 entries and compete for 58 prizes worth $102K. Make Your Picks Now, let's get to some prop bets ... Rashee Rice receiving yards OVER 47.5 (-114) Rice, who caught four of six targets for 83 yards in the Week 2 win over the Colts, could have early opportunities against the Dolphins' single-high man coverages. Rice can turn an underneath throw into an explosive gain. Travis Kelce receptions OVER 4.5 receptions (-114) Kelce's play speed looked different last week against the Colts, both in the route stem and after the catch. Kelce caught nine of 11 targets in that game, using his high-end coverage awareness to find open grass. He should be a priority target again for Mahomes on Sunday. Tyquan Thornton anytime TD (+475) I'm thinking of a shot-play throw here to Thornton on Sunday. Thornton caught all four of his targets for 86 yards last week against the Colts, so look for Reid to set up him on a deep-ball concept in Miami. Not one of WR Zay Flowers , OT Ronnie Stanley or OLB Trey Hendrickson practiced Wednesday for the Ravens. Still, head coach Jesse Minter said after practice that he feels "like we will have a good shot with a lot of guys this week." Editor's Picks Top predicted anytime TD scorers for Week 3 Mike Clay NFL Week 3 betting: Odds, lines and totals for every game NFL awards: Purdy hot on Burrow's heels in MVP race Doug Greenberg 2 Related Assuming the Ravens are relatively close to full strength, I like their matchup against Dallas quite a bit. The Cowboys' back seven has struggled tremendously through two weeks of the Christian Parker era on defense; it's a challenging defensive scheme, and they are generally lacking for team speed. Their light edge rushers can be targeted in the run game. Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has excelled at two things so far: attacking the edge in the running game, and generating YAC opportunities for Flowers. Baltimore might steamroll the Cowboys. I'm a little worried about the travel and field in Brazil, which can introduce some chaos. The Cowboys' offense can also score in bunches. But the Ravens are a better pressure team, thanks to the play of Hendrickson and Minter's willingness to send pressures on key downs. I like them to get enough stops in what should be a high-scoring affair. I'd take this up to -4 (-110), but only if we get positive injury news throughout the week. Houston Texans -1.5 (-118) at Indianapolis Colts Two 0-2 division rivals seemingly with their seasons already on the line -- intense stuff for Week 3. I admired the Colts' pluck in their game against the Chiefs, but the Texans' defense is made of far stiffer stuff. Houston has won the last five games between the teams, though QB Daniel Jones was hurt for the most recent matchup. NFL Win Totals Predict OVER or UNDER for every team's win total. FREE to play. $5K in prizes! Make Your Picks The Colts have relied heavily on big-play receiver Alec Pierce to generate explosive plays against DeMeco Ryans' aggressive defense. Last season against the Texans across two games, Pierce had eight catches, 210 yards and three touchdowns. Pierce hurt his heel against the Chiefs and is on injured reserve, which puts all the more pressure on Josh Downs , Keenan Allen and Laquon Treadwell at receiver. It's hard to imagine the Colts finding the same big plays that the Buffalo Bills and Cincinnati Bengals have against this Texans secondary. It looks like star receiver Nico Collins will miss another week with a hamstring injury, which has pulled this line down to -1.5 after opening at -2.5 and flirting with -3 throughout the week. I'm still on the Texans' side here -- their offense moved the ball much better against Cincinnati defense than the scoreboard would indicate (35.1% success rate was far better than the Bengals' 27.6% on the day). The Colts' linebacker room is such a liability that I expect C.J. Stroud to still have a strong day working the middle of the field. David Montgomery anytime TD (-110), 2+ TD scorer (+550) I'm thrilled to get Montgomery back down near even money after the Texans' absolute stinker against the Bengals in Week 2. Montgomery's number is low this week out of fear of another inept offensive day without Collins, but the Texans weren't all that bad on offense. One drive ended at the Bengals' 16-yard line on a fumbled field goal try. Another ended on the Bengals' 18 on a fourth-and-1 run failure. Another resulted in a field goal from the Bengals' 19, a fearful attempt on fourth-and-1 as the Bengals were dominating in short yardage. So, the Texans moved the ball a lot more effectively than the scoreboard would indicate. They'll be much better in short yardage when they don't have DT Dexter Lawrence II to face -- and, in general, they should find easier offense against a young and leaky Colts defense. We already know that once the Texans are in the red zone, they mash the Montgomery button aggressively -- doubly so, I'd imagine, if Collins can't go. I have a unit on 1+ touchdown and a quarter-unit on two touchdowns at +550, which I wouldn't take any lower than +530. Trey McBride and the Cardinals' offense could pose some matchup problems for the 49ers. Gary A. Vasquez/Imagn Images Arizona Cardinals +8.5 (-112) at San Francisco 49ers These are two teams about which, I'd argue, we still know very little. The 49ers got the sleepy Los Angeles Rams in Week 1 Down Under and trounced them thoroughly. They drew the listless Dolphins in Week 2 and gave them the business as well. I have no doubt the 49ers are a good team, but how good is unclear -- and they've gotten even more banged up in the interim. DT C.J. West is going on injured reserve, and WR Demarcus Robinson is expected to sit out time because of a high-ankle sprain. Behind Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel Sr ., the 49ers are perilously thin at wide receiver. Of course, the Cardinals have their own injuries at corner ( Will Johnson , Max Melton , Garrett Williams ), but they're a heavy zone team anyway and can hide those issues more easily. The Cardinals got the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 1, and that win looked good ... until we saw the Chargers in Week 2. Arizona's offense got punked by Mike Macdonald and the Seattle Seahawks defense, but I've seen elite offenses struggle against that group. I still suspect this is a perfectly average offense, and the 49ers' defense is still a suspiciously young and thin group. I think the Cardinals get a good ground game going that shortens this contest and keeps it within a touchdown. Even if the 49ers get an early lead, I don't think they have a great answer for TE Trey McBride . If they pull LB Fred Warner out of the middle of the field to stick with the tight end in man coverage, Jacoby Brissett and Mike LaFleur will start spamming in-breakers. I'd take this to +8. Emmett Johnson rushing + receiving yards OVER 38.5 (-114) NFL Playoff Predictor Predict the final standings in every division, then choose which teams will earn a wild-card berth! FREE to play. Make Your Picks Johnson, a fifth-round rookie running back out of Nebraska, is the clear RB2 behind Kenneth Walker III, and he has been explosive in limited usage (39 yards on 10 carries and 64 yards on four receptions). He's an aggressive, upfield runner who seeks contact and sheds it well -- and, because he can contribute on both running and receiving downs, he's a good foil to Walker. The Chiefs are double-digit favorites over the Dolphins in Miami this Sunday, and in a blowout script, we can anticipate Johnson gets a heavy dose of running game usage. He has been more effective as a dump-off player, so I like taking his rushing and receiving yards here as a protection against game script and overall efficiency. If he runs into loaded boxes in a lopsided second half and doesn't accumulate yardage, or if the game ends up oddly close, he still can pop a big reception against the passive Dolphins defense and still get home. I would take this line up to 40 yards, and I'd consider overs on rushing attempts as well when that posts. KC Concepcion receiving yards OVER 32.5 (-112) I'm back to the well on Concepcion, who burned us last week with only 29 yards on six receptions. The Cleveland Browns had a couple of downfield plays dialed up for Concepcion, whom they continued to use in enticing ways from the slot and in motion, but they never got the ball in the air. Still, we have a player getting designed touches in the screen game and who is the safety valve underneath and is also still running vertical routes, with an average route depth (12.4) just below the league average for WRs (13.0). I see no reason to fade Concepcion's route totals, especially against a Carolina Panthers defense that has faced only one real offense so far this year (and gave up 59 points when they did so). The Browns are also always liable to enter a big negative game script, which should funnel easy targets. Fool me once, shame on you. Fool me twice, shame on me. Concepcion will get home this week. I'd take the number up to 34.5. Bo Nix rushing yards UNDER 17.5 (-111) Your League, Your Rules Create a league and customize league size, scoring and rules to play in the league you want to play in. Create a league today! There has been only one scramble through two games for Nix in 2026, which is notable, as Nix was scrambling 2.3 times per game in 2025. It doesn't seem to be related to the ankle injury -- he's moving just fine -- so my theory is that it's related to the new Davis Webb offensive approach. Either the Broncos brass has stressed upon him the importance of putting the ball in play, or Nix is more comfortable with the playcalls as they're given to him and is less likely to cut bait to tuck and go. Whatever it is, I'll take his under on his rushing yards against the Rams. With the litany of RB injuries the Broncos have, I think the Rams will be willing to play Nix's keeps on read-option a little more aggressively. I also expect the Rams to be a heavy zone team in this game despite the shift to man coverage in Week 2. Nix has historically been a much shakier passer against zone than man coverage. Zone coverage allows defenders to keep their eyes on scrambling quarterbacks, which limits yardage on the hoof. I wouldn't take the number any lower than this -- just one big run could get us in trouble at such a small figure. Geno Smith 2+ passing TDs (+157) There's huge familiarity here between Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell and New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn, who was Campbell's defensive coordinator in Detroit for three seasons. Glenn's linebackers coach, Kelvin Sheppard, has replaced him and runs a similar, but slightly more versatile defense. Still, I expect Glenn to have a good bead on the things that will give Sheppard trouble, especially in spots where coverage gets predictable -- like the red zone. Detroit's defense plays with heavier boxes than any defense in football, so I expect a lot of dropbacks for Smith. With Mason Taylor out because of a wrist injury, the Jets have also lost their primary in-line tight end, and I think the rushing efficiency is going to suffer. Of all the Smith overs I'm interested in this week, I'll take 2+ passing touchdowns at this long of a number. Smith has thrown only one TD pass, but the Jets are 53.3% pass in the red zone through two games (right around league average). They aren't hiding him at this part of the field. Ben Solak 2026 best bets record Category Record Unit change Spread 5-9 -4.4 Total 1-2 -1.1 Passing props 8-5 +3.5 Receiving props 6-12 -6.6 Rushing props 8-2 +5.3 Rushing and receiving props 0-1 -1.0 Touchdown props 1-2 -1.1 Overall 29-33 -5.6 Walder's prop bets Kyler Murray will make his return Sunday after recovering from a concussion sustained in Week 1. Jeffrey Becker/Imagn Images Note: More defensive props will be added as odds become available Defensive plays Chargers to NOT allow a sack on first drive (-311) Everything is bad with the Chargers. But it's not this bad. For context, the same bet for the Bills is -482. Even the Commanders, similarly-sized underdogs with a backup quarterback going against an elite Seattle defense, are -349 this week. So, at -311, I see the Chargers as a value. And though the Chargers being big underdogs increases the chance of Justin Herbert getting sacked during the game, that effect is mitigated early on. The Chargers won't be forced into a desperate must-pass situation on their first drive. Plus, the Bills rank just 27th in pass rush win rate, which further lowers the probability of a first-drive sack. Derrick Brown UNDER 0.25 sacks (-140) The first sack bet I listed in this column all year was betting against Deshaun Watson and his incredibly high sack rate. He has continued taking sacks at an incredible clip ... on 11.9% of his dropbacks this season. So why bet under? Because for every bet there's a price where it makes sense. And -140 is a price where I'm willing to fade Brown, even in a tantalizing matchup against Cleveland and Watson. Brown is a good player but taking down the quarterback is not his primary skill: he has just 13.0 sacks in his career. And he's actually rushing the passer a little less frequently this season than last year. I would bet this all the way down to -210. A'Shawn Robinson UNDER 0.25 sacks (-388) This might be the least fun bet recommended in this column all year. But value is value! And I'll bet it at all any part along the odds spectrum. Robinson has just 16.0 sacks since he entered the league in 2016, and I think he's particularly unlikely to get No. 17 in this game. That's because of when he's playing. The Bucs have had Robinson on the field on just 23% of clear pass rushing situations this season, down from 52% last year in Carolina. Other sack bets I recommend: Jaelan Phillips UNDER 0.75 sacks (+125) Leonard Williams UNDER 0.25 sacks (-109) Chris Jones UNDER 0.25 sacks (-138) Andrew Van Ginkel UNDER 0.25 sacks (-128) Donovan Ezeiruaku UNDER 4.5 tackles + assists (-107) Ezeiruaku has been playing a little more this season -- 65% of snaps this year vs. 55% last year -- but that's not nearly enough to overcome this high line for an edge rusher. I think what's happening here is this line is being inflated by an outlandish 10-tackle game in Week 1. But it was only the third time Ezeiruaku had ever gone over 4.5 combined tackles in his career. If Ezeiruaku's role had changed substantially in addition to the slight uptick in playing time this would be a different story, but he's still playing as a 7 or 9 technique 93% of the time (was 89% last year). And Ezeiruaku's tackle rate was almost exactly average for an edge rusher last year. I think the under here is an excellent value. Jordyn Brooks UNDER 9.5 tackles + assists (-116) It's pretty easy to imagine how Brooks could accrue a gaudy tackle number in this game. The Chiefs are double-digit favorites, have been having success with the ground game and if they get out to a big lead they'll simply run the ball to run out the clock. The result? Plenty of tackle opportunities for Miami's defense, and in particular a linebacker like Brooks. But the model knows all that and says this line is just far too high. Just last week Miami was massive underdogs to the 49ers and Brooks recorded just three combined tackles. I would bet this down to -150. Offensive plays Kyler Murray interceptions UNDER 0.5 (+121) The thing to know about forecasting interceptions is how close to 50/50 the baseline expectation for the average quarterback in the average game is. So when we see a +121 line for the under, that usually indicates a poor quarterback and/or a heavy underdog. I don't think Murray is that. Whatever you think of Murray -- and, I'll admit, I've long been a little more bullish on him than consensus -- he has been very consistent in terms of his interception rate, ranging between 1.6% and 1.8% each of his four previous seasons, all at or a little better than average. During that span, he never had a dropped interception, either. Add in that the Minnesota Vikings are favored and my model doesn't see why Murray should to be priced this way. I would bet this down to +105. Bryce Young pass attempts UNDER 33.5 (-124) The Carolina Panthers have been surprisingly pass-happy through the first two weeks of the season, with a plus-4% pass rate over expectation, according to NFL Next Gen Stats, fifth highest in the NFL. That's a massive departure from last year, when Carolina was negative 8% and ranked 31st in the same category. This bet hinges on whether what we've seen thus far continues. My attempts model is betting not. And there's also another quite simple path to a win here: If the Panthers simply blow out the Browns early -- and that's always possible when you're facing Deshaun Watson -- they'll rely on the run game in the second half. By Vaughn Dalzell , By Vaughn Dalzell Published November 22, 2026 10:05 AM Add on Google Facebook Twitter Email Add on Google After a hot 4-1 Thursday Night, let’s have a winning Sunday! Here are my eight best bets for the day. Best of luck! Game odds are courtesy of DraftKings . Titans at Cowboys (-7.5): O/U 54.5 The Titans and Cowboys meet in a battle of two of the worst defenses in the NFL. The Titans are 4-0 to the Over in the last four games, while the Cowboys are 3-1 to the Over in that same span. Dallas is 7-3 to the Over on the year, and Tennessee is 6-3, both ranking top five. The Titans and Cowboys have allowed opponents to score on 46% of drives, ranking 30th and 31st, and both allow a passing success rate of 50% or higher, ranking 29th and 31st — you get the drift. Totals of 54 or higher in the last three seasons are 14-4 to the Over. This one has the making of at least one team reaching 30 points. I like the Over 54.5 up to 55.5. Lean Tennessee +7.5 as they’ve drawn sharp money. Pick: Over 54.5 (1 unit) Jared Goff O/U 32.5 Pass Attempts vs Buccaneers Now that Baker Mayfield is in, we are back on Jared Goff’s passing attempts over 32.5. He would have likely cashed the over 34.5 last week against New England, but Drake Maye’s injury threw off the entire game flow. With Mayfield in, plus the Buccaneers defense being capable of offering resistance in the rush game, this is a good spot for Goff to go over after under his passing attempts in five-straight games. The Bucs run the eighth-most zone coverage at 79.2%, and Goff ranks top 10 in completion percentage (71%), passer rating (100.8), and catchable rate (76.9%) against zone coverage. I’d go up to 33.5. Pick: Jared Goff Over 32.5 Pass Attempts (1.5 units) Patrick Mahomes O/U 30.5 Pass Attempts vs Cardinals Much like Matthew Stafford and the Rams last week, I don’t expect many passes to be thrown in the second half on the Chiefs side. Stafford threw three passes in the third quarter and none in the fourth as the Rams waxed the Cardinals 34-6. With a spread of -15.5, it’s safe to say the Chiefs should be in a positive game script, meaning most of Patrick Mahomes ’ damage will come in the first half. Mahomes threw for 348 yards and a season-high five touchdowns against Atlanta on 22-of-35 (62.9%). The Chiefs’ offense is pretty depleted, and despite not having Kenneth Walker , Emmett Johnson proved he can handle the bulk of the ground work. I like Mahomes to go under 30.5 pass attempts to 29.5. This opened at 31.5. Pick: Patrick Mahomes Under 30.5 Pass Attempts (1 unit) Saquon Barkley O/U 55.5 Rushing Yards vs Steelers Steelers versus Eagles smells like an Under and an offensive struggle. Saquon Barkley ’s props have moved on the move downward over the last few days. This situation is similar to Jonathan Taylo r and the Colts; much like Taylor, Barkley’s snap share and usage will continue to decline as the Eagles lose more games and save him for next season. Barkley had a 58% snap share last week, marking the third time he’s crossed 50%. It won’t happen that often the rest of the season. With less snaps equals less opportunities. The best bet is fading Saquon every week, and I have to lean toward fading the Eagles until they start covering. At 1-8 ATS and 7 straight outright losses. Maybe the bye week helped them, but I doubt it. Pick: Saquon Barkley Under 55.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Saints at Bears (-11.5): O/U 48.5 Chicago coming out of a bye week is certainly an appealing bet-on team. The offense has been cooking with 31, 30, 34, and 27 points since Caleb Williams returned. Those games came against some pretty good defenses too: the Falcons, Patriots, Seahawks, and Buccaneers. The Saints have only allowed three teams to reach 30 points on them: the Lions, Raiders, and Falcons. Better yet, the Saints have played some mediocre passing attacks in the last four games: Bryce Young , Shedeur Sanders , Aaron Rodgers , and Jameis Winston . I don’t think that group has prepared the Saints’ defense for what they’re about to face. The last factor: the Saints are 3-0 ATS on the road this year, but two of those road games came in Weeks 1-2, and the other on October 18 (Week 6). The Saints have either been at home or in Paris in seven of the past eight games. This will be a tough road contest, and if you fall behind early, I don’t think New Orleans could dig themselves out, so I like Chicago -11.5, but love the team total over 29.5 up to 30.5. Pick: Bears Team Total Over 29.5 (1 unit) Rotoworld still has you covered with all the latest and tools for the NFL, including game predictions, player props, futures, and trends! Cam Skattebo O/U 54.5 Rushing Yards vs. Jaguars Cam Skattebo has one of the trap lines of the week. Skattebo recorded 58 or more in six out of seven games he’s received a carry, and posted 124 and 78 in the last two games. This is one of those stinker lines in general; only if the Giants can keep this within a two-possession game could Skattebo hit the over. The Jaguars have a tendency to make teams abandon the run when they start to fall behind. Similar to Tony Pollard with the Titans last week, he was on a mini-monster run, and they were hanging a line that he crushed all season, but went way under versus the Jaguars with nine carries and 33 yards. Pollard had eight receptions on nine targets for 66 yards and a touchdown. I think the Giants’ backs will be important to the pass game because it’s going to be hard to avoid obvious passing or rushing situations. I like Skattebo to go under 54.5 rushing yards, down to 51.5. Pick: Cam Skattebo Under 54.5 Rushing Yards (1 unit) Raiders at Broncos (-10.5): O/U 40.5 I was most impressed with that Vegas opening drive last week, getting Fernando Mendoza comfortable and using his famous Indiana draw play to get his first NFL touchdown, of course, without the twisting and contorting. This week, I would look for a slow start and a lack of points from the Raiders offense, especially after the Brock Bowers injury. Bowers barely practiced on Thursday and is fighting to play, but if he is out, I don’t know if anyone saw the second half last week. The Raiders had -2 yards of offense on 3 drives in the second quarter, and -15 yards on the first two drives of the fourth quarter before moving the ball down the field for a field goal to lose by eight. It was horrible. Denver is a top-six first-quarter and first-half defense in PPG at 2.7 and 8.8. I could only look at either backing the Broncos on the first-quarter or first-half spreads, or taking the Under on the Raiders 1Q and 1H Team Totals. I will start with the Broncos first quarter -2.5. Denver has scored in five of the last six first quarters, and Las Vegas has trailed in three of five first quarters on the road — the two they didn’t were against the Jets (led 7-6) and Chargers (tied 0-0). Pick: Broncos 1Q -2.5 (1 unit) Vikings vs 49ers (-3.5): O/U 46.5 Brock Purdy goes from playing Dallas, which is one of the worst defenses in the NFL, to playing Minnesota in Mexico City. The Vikings have one of the best defenses in the NFL, and the altitude and location could throw these teams off a bit, specifically San Francisco. Mike Evans is questionable, and if he’s out, I really like the Under 46.5 in this matchup. The 49ers have hit the over game total five times this season against the Cowboys, Raiders, Cardinals, Dolphins, and Seahawks. Four of those make a ton of sense. The Vikings wouldn’t. The Vikings are an NFL-best 8-1 to the Under, 5-0 to the Under as an underdog, and 5-0 to the Under in non-division games. The last over was in Week 1, so we might as well keep riding the Under at eight straight wins. Pick: Under 46.5 (1 unit) Weeks 1-6: 29-42 (40.8%) -15.95 units Weeks 7-9: 34-14 (70.8%) +19 units Week 10: 10-9 +0.66 units Week 11: 4-1 +2.62 units Week 11 Picks 1.5 units: Jared Goff Over 32.5 Pass Attempts (-120) 1 unit: Chicago Bears Team Total Over 29.5 (-135) 1 unit: Cowboys vs Titans Over 54.5 (-117) 1 unit: Patrick Mahomes Under 30.5 Pass Attempts (-102) 1 unit: Saquon Barkley Under 55.5 Rushing Yards (-114) 1 unit: Cam Skattebo Under 54.5 Rushing Yards (-113) 1 unit: Broncos 1Q -2.5 (-122) 1 unit: Vikings vs 49ers Under 46.5 (-114) Please bet responsibly.
